## Cross-Pod Dependencies

- Config endpoints gated by RBAC permissions (config:read/write/delete)
- Sessions pod needs Locales config for multi-language support

conflicts.summary: Config inheritance model: full-replace (child completely overrides parent) vs. deep-merge (child overrides individual fields)

sides.position: Full-replace inheritance. The ConfigService is already built with full-replace semantics — when a team-level scope has RSVP config, it completely replaces the org-level RSVP config. This is simpler to reason about, easier to debug, and avoids merge ambiguity for ordered lists like custom attribute values. The 5-minute cache TTL and request deduplication are built around this model.

Deep-merge inheritance. Event organizers want to add a few custom fields at the team level without re-specifying all 15 base RSVP fields from the org level. Full-replace means every team must duplicate the org config and add their changes — this is error-prone and creates config drift when the org updates base fields.

conflicts.master_analysis: Fundamental architectural decision. be-agent-configs has a working implementation with full-replace. pm-configs raises a valid UX concern about config duplication and drift. Deep-merge would require: (1) rewriting ConfigService resolution logic, (2) defining merge rules for each config type, (3) handling ordered-list merges for custom attribute values. This is blocking because the frontend config editor UI depends on knowing whether users are editing a full config or a delta overlay.
impact: Custom attribute ordering depends on inheritance model

conflicts.summary: ConfigService cache: 5-minute TTL with deduplication vs. real-time invalidation via webhooks

sides.position: 5-minute TTL cache with request deduplication and 2 retries on miss. Simple, predictable, already implemented. Config changes are infrequent (~3 times per day per scope) so a 5-minute delay is acceptable. Real-time invalidation adds infrastructure complexity (webhook registration, event bus, cache-key targeting).

Config changes should be visible immediately in the UI. An admin editing RSVP fields expects to see the changes reflected in the preview immediately, not up to 5 minutes later. At minimum, the editing user's session should invalidate its cache on write. Other users can tolerate the TTL.

conflicts.master_analysis: Non-blocking because the config CRUD endpoints work regardless of cache behavior. fe-agent-configs has a valid point about the editing UX. A pragmatic middle ground: keep the 5-minute TTL for cross-session reads, but add a write-through cache bust for the current user's session. This avoids the infrastructure overhead of webhooks while solving the immediate UX issue.
impact: Config editor UX for admins making changes
No impact on end-user-facing config reads

nodes.summary: ESP event-speaker PUT body contract is { speakerId, speakerType, ordinal, creationTime, modificationTime } and nothing else
nodes.details: Per ESP OpenAPI, /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId PUT accepts only those five fields. Echoing the full GET response (spreading dependentData) fails server-side validation and has been the root cause of repeated 400s on edit. When using callWithDependency's body-builder, fall back to dependentData per-field: body.X ?? dependentData.X. creationTime and modificationTime are server-issued; do not let callers override them. The same pattern applies to all ESP PUTs on speaker resources.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: Response validation must be permissive for legacy attendee data; request-side validation is decoupled and handled separately by RSVP forms.
nodes.details: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField schemas in GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees responses were over-constrained (pattern: ^\+?[0-9]+$, maxLength: 20 for phone; pattern rejecting all HTML for text fields with maxLength: 100), causing 12.8% of production attendee records to fail HTTP 418 validation. The fix relaxes response schemas (PhoneNumber: drop pattern, maxLength 30; AttendeeTextField: newline-tolerant pattern ^(?![\s\S]*<[^>]*>)[\s\S]*$, maxLength 200) while explicitly documenting that form-side input validation remains the responsibility of RSVP-form frontends. This resolves the architectural tension: the service layer must accept and return legacy data as-is; sanitization and strict validation belong upstream.

nodes.summary: Scope configs unify RSVP forms, locales, and custom attributes under a single typed config system with scope-inherited hierarchy (org → team) and full-replace merge semantics.
nodes.details: All configuration for the events console — RSVP form fields, locale definitions, and custom attribute definitions — is managed through a single `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs` API with `type` field (e.g., 'rsvp', 'locales', 'custom-attributes'). Configs inherit down the scope hierarchy with full-replace merge per type. Frontend reads merged configs via `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs` or `GET /v1/series/{seriesId}/configs` with optional `?type=` filter. Custom attributes are a config type, not a separate entity. Admin management uses POST/PUT/DELETE on `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs/{configId}` and requires `config:read`, `config:write`, or `config:delete` permissions.

nodes.summary: Scope configs (rsvp, locales, customAttributes) are the authoritative source for event metadata; publishing profiles are deprecated but retained for backward compatibility during migration.
nodes.details: Events created under Creative Events (25f26faa-f8e2-4e99-b341-81a3995ef9af) and Enterprise Events (d758a3bc-ff31-4bfe-a2f5-343f074aec6c) scopes must define four config types: rsvp (pool of form fields), locales (localeNames, localeUrlCodes), and customAttributes (with primaryProductName and promotionalItems attributes). The Kinesis processor (events-kinesis-processor/ServiceProcessor.applyRelatedData) must call GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs to hydrate event.locales, event.customAttributesConfig, and event.rsvpConfig at stream-processing time; event DDB records store only user selections (rsvpFormFields, customAttributes[] with valueId), not full definitions. Publishing profiles remain in the payload for backward compat but are no longer the source of truth. hoolihan-webhooks must read primary product from event.customAttributes[] where attribute='primaryProductName', promotional items from customAttributes[] where attribute='promotionalItems', RSVP pool from event.rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields[], and locales from event.locales.localeNames/localeUrlCodes.

nodes.summary: ESL must mirror ESP's AttendeeTextField relaxations (maxLength 100→200, newline-tolerant regex) to avoid being a stricter validation gate than upstream, preventing legacy attendee data from passing re-validation.
nodes.details: When ESL re-validates attendee payloads against its own OpenAPI spec, fields like `invitedBy` and `campaignId` (both typed as `AttendeeTextField`) must accept the same input that ESP accepts. The original pattern `^(?!.*<[^>]*>).*$` rejected newlines; the relaxed pattern `^(?![\s\S]*<[^>]*>)[\s\S]*$` accepts them. maxLength was raised from 100 to 200 characters. This is not a feature expansion—it is a compatibility fix to unblock legacy data that ESP already accepts. Do not selectively port only some field relaxations from ESP; ESL's `BaseAttendee` / `EventAttendee` schemas define which fields exist, and only those should be relaxed (e.g., `PhoneNumber` is unreferenced in ESL and should not be changed).

nodes.summary: Do not spread GET response into PUT body; construct narrow association payloads with only required fields plus timestamps.
nodes.details: In `web-src/src/services/api.ts`, `updateSpeakerInEvent` previously merged the full GET response (minus `creationTime`) into the PUT body, sending unintended fields to ESP. The corrected pattern: construct PUT payloads with only `speakerId`, `speakerType`, `ordinal` (from caller patch with GET fallbacks when omitted), plus `creationTime` and `modificationTime` from GET. This matches the documented ESP contract and the existing `updateSponsorInEvent` pattern. Callers like the Speakers dashboard may send partial patches (e.g., only `speakerId`); the service must fill missing association fields from the prior GET before PUT.

nodes.summary: RSVP contactMethods field must not be spread directly from GET response into PUT payload; use prepareContactMethodsForPut helper to normalize shape.
nodes.details: The events-form block's RSVP submission was spreading the GET response contactMethods array directly into the PUT body, causing server-side validation failures when field shapes diverged between read and write contracts. The fix introduces a normalization step (prepareContactMethodsForPut in event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js) that maps the GET schema to the PUT schema before submission. This pattern applies to all ESP PUT operations: never assume GET and PUT payloads have identical field structures; always use a prepare* helper to bridge the contract gap.

nodes.summary: RSVP button and form 400-error handling must respect campaign capacity when ?campaign URL param is present and valid, falling back to event capacity otherwise, with campaign-specific error messages and UI state.
nodes.details: When a valid campaign ID is present in the URL (?campaign=...), use getCampaign() to fetch campaign capacity and apply it to both RSVP button state (updateRSVPButtonState in decorate.js) and form 400-error handling (buildErrorMsg and submit handler in events-form.js). If campaign fetch fails or campaign ID is invalid (validate via CAMPAIGN_ID_PATTERN in constances.js), fall back to event capacity. On 400 response with campaign present, use campaign-full-error-msg or campaign-full-no-waitlist-error-msg keys and update submit button to waitlist or event-full state (disabled if no waitlist) to keep copy and UI consistent. This ensures campaign-level capacity gates take precedence over event-level gates when applicable.

nodes.summary: Manager classes in events-service-platform automatically persist request body fields via spread operator; schema changes alone are sufficient for new optional fields without code changes.
nodes.details: The `sponsorsMgr.js` manager spreads the full request body into `itemData` during POST/PUT operations, meaning any new optional field added to OpenAPI schemas (e.g., `ordinal` in EventSponsorCreateBody, EventSponsorUpdateBody) is automatically persisted and returned without requiring manager code changes. This pattern applies to sponsor creation, updates, and retrieval. When adding optional fields to event entities, verify the manager uses spread semantics before adding schema-only changes.

nodes.summary: Event attendee route handlers use explicit field mappings instead of spreading req.body, causing OpenAPI-validated fields to silently drop before persistence.
nodes.details: The attendee CRUD routes (create.js, update.js, read.js) in src/routes/events/attendees/ build eventAttendee objects by hand-picking fields rather than spreading req.body. This means fields validated by the OpenAPI spec (e.g., requiresTicket) can pass validation but never reach DynamoDB or the response. When adding a new attendee field, it must be explicitly added to all three route handlers' field mappings, or it will be silently dropped. Use explicit field mappings only when you need to exclude or transform fields; otherwise, spread req.body and filter at the schema layer.

nodes.summary: Do not apply strict input validation schemas to GET response bodies; use separate input and output schemas to preserve backward compatibility with legacy data.
nodes.details: In events-service-platform, attendee phone fields (`mobilePhone`, `businessPhone`) must support two schemas: a strict `PhoneNumberInput` pattern `^[+\d\s\-().]+$` for POST/PUT writes, and a permissive `PhoneNumber` schema for GET responses. Implement this via OpenAPI `allOf` composition on request bodies (`requestBodies/BaseAttendee`, `requestBodies/Attendee`) while keeping response schemas unchanged. This prevents validation errors on legacy data (e.g. `"None"`, `"N/A"`) that exists in the database but should not be accepted on new writes. See `src/api/openapi.json` for the schema structure and `src/api/test/openapi-attendees-validation.test.js` for validation test patterns.

nodes.summary: Localization Kinesis records omit non-localization fields like rsvpFormFields; always fetch the full event record before scope filtering when hydrating from a localization change.
nodes.details: In ServiceProcessor.js, when a localization record change triggers `callHydratedEvent` with `forceSpWrite=true`, the hydrated payload lacks `rsvpFormFields` because Kinesis localization records only carry localization-scoped fields. The full event record (sk: event) must be fetched via `eventService.getEventData()` before scope config filtering runs, otherwise `rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields` will be empty. Check for `forceSpWrite && !rsvpFormFields` to gate this parallel fetch and avoid redundant calls on non-localization event modifications.

nodes.summary: When hydrating event payloads from DynamoDB kinesis records with sk=localizations, source seriesId and detailPagePath from the pre-fetched liveData object, not from newData.itemData (which lacks these fields).
nodes.details: In EventDataStreamProcessor.js, when processing a localization record change (sk=localizations), the newData.itemData payload contains only localizations and localizationOverrides. To build a complete hydrated event for ESL, pull seriesId and detailPagePath from liveData (fetched via eventService.getEventData at processRecord start), not from newData.itemData. This is safe because EventService.updateVenue writes the new detailPagePath to DynamoDB before the venue record fires the kinesis stream, ensuring liveData.detailPagePath is current. Omitting these fields causes DA webhook page creation to fail or write to wrong locations.

nodes.summary: Attendees resource has dual CRUD surfaces: standalone /v1/attendees/* for lifecycle management, and nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* for event-specific membership operations only.
nodes.details: The attendees CRUD operations split across two route hierarchies: /v1/attendees/{create,read,update,delete}.js handle attendee entity lifecycle (create new attendee, read attendee details, update attendee profile, delete attendee). The nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* routes (in src/routes/events/attendees/) handle only event membership: POST adds an *existing* attendee to an event (does not create attendees), GET lists attendees for an event, DELETE removes attendee from event, PUT updates attendee's event-specific state. This separation prevents attendee creation from being coupled to event enrollment. Enforce via attendeesMgr.js and eventsMgr.js: standalone routes call attendeesMgr directly; nested routes validate attendee exists before calling eventsMgr membership methods.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The fix: in useEventFormSave.ts, call dataFilters to set detailPagePath.submittable = true before the PUT, and detect title changes to trigger the DA page path dialog. This requires coordinated backend changes to the OpenAPI spec to allow the field in PUT requests. The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: Event-attendee payload fields must be explicitly listed in EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER to be sent to ESL's addAttendeeToEvent endpoint.
nodes.details: The EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in event-libs/v1/utils/data-utils.js acts as an allowlist for which form fields are included in the event-attendee payload sent to ESL. New checkbox or form fields (e.g., requiresSxswTicket, shareInfoWithPartners) must be added to this filter in getEventAttendeePayload() to be transmitted. Additionally, when gating form fields via rsvp-form-fields metadata in events-form.js, new sheet fields must be listed in the visible array to render; unlisted fields are silently dropped.

nodes.summary: Campaign-aware RSVP registration: when campaignId URL param is present, fetch campaign capacity and apply waitlist rules before attendee creation.
nodes.details: In esp-controller.js, the getAndCreateAndAddAttendee flow checks for campaignId in the attendee payload. If present and event is not full, call getCampaign(eventId, campaignId) to fetch campaign capacity (attendeeLimit, attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount). Apply waitlist logic: if attendeeLimit === attendeeCount, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount > 0, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount === 0, register normally. If no attendeeLimit, pass campaignId without campaign logic. Skip campaign lookup when event is already full. campaignId is sanitized in events-form.js (regex ^[\w-]{1,128}$) and added to EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in data-utils.js so it flows into the event attendee API body.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: Speakers and sponsors are grouped by role/tier with per-group drag-and-drop reordering; role/tier changes move items to the end of the new group and trigger per-group ordinal recomputation.
nodes.details: In SpeakersComponent.tsx and SponsorsComponent.tsx, items are grouped by speakerType and tier respectively. Drag-and-drop is restricted to within-group moves only (cross-group drops are blocked). When a speaker's role or sponsor's tier is changed via inline picker, the item is moved to the end of the new group. On save, onAfterSave computes per-group ordinals for both components. SponsorData now includes an optional ordinal field, and updateSponsorInEvent in api.ts explicitly preserves ordinal in the merge logic. Both components display a disclaimer note that group display order on the DA page is governed by template configuration, not EMC form ordering.

nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: CSV export filename convention: prefix with event title and ISO datetime, sanitize user input, append .csv extension only at download time.
nodes.details: EMC attendee and campaign exports use a standardized filename pattern: `[event-title]_[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS]` for attendees, `[event-title]_campaigns_[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS]` for campaigns. The `utils/csvExport.ts` module provides `sanitizeFilename()` and `exportDatetime()` helpers to enforce this. Filenames are user-editable in the export dialog but must be sanitized before download; `.csv` extension is appended at download time, not stored in the user-facing field. This pattern applies across ExportDialog.tsx (attendee) and CampaignExportDialog (campaign tab).

nodes.summary: EMC migrated from sidebar to top navigation (gnav) layout; TopNav component in SideBar.tsx with UserPanel compact mode; App.tsx grid changed from ['sidebar', 'content'] to ['header', 'content'] with rows ['auto', '1fr'].
nodes.details: The layout shift encodes a durable architectural pattern: (1) SideBar.tsx was repurposed as TopNav with horizontal nav items and brand logo on left, user panel on right; (2) UserPanel.tsx gained a `compact` prop that hides email/org and reduces avatar size for header context; (3) App.tsx grid layout changed from 2-column sidebar model to 2-row header model with grid areas ['header', 'content'] and rows ['auto', '1fr']; (4) Navigation links use `.nav-link` class with bottom border (3px solid transparent) for active state, not background highlight; (5) Content area must have `gridArea='content'` and overflow scroll enabled. This pattern is reusable for any future layout refactors and clarifies the component responsibility split.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: POI (point of interest) must not be auto-hydrated into event objects for SharePoint push; responsibility lies with event marketers and FE validation.
nodes.details: PR #633 attempted to add POI to hydrated event objects in ServiceProcessor.js (aws/templates/lambda/events-kinesis-processor/src/ServiceProcessor.js) for SharePoint sync. This was reverted because: (1) event marketers are responsible for consciously excluding POI from form field selections during event creation, and (2) the EMC console FE (owned by Qiyun) provides safeguarding at RSVP field selection, where POI option visibility is already controlled. Do not auto-inject POI into the event hydration pipeline; enforce the contract that POI inclusion is an explicit, user-driven choice at form design time.

nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: Session-time helpers must return SessionTimeInfo so React state can update without a page refresh
nodes.details: createSessionTimeForSession and upsertSessionTimeForSession previously returned Promise<void>, which dropped the API's sessionTimeId, creationTime, and modificationTime on the floor. Calling components could not update local state with the new optimistic-concurrency values, so users saw stale data and had to refresh the page after every session-time edit. Fix is to return the API response from both helpers and have handleAddSession / handleUpdateSession capture and propagate sessionTimeId + creationTime + modificationTime into local React session state. This is the EMC-wide convention for any API helper that yields server-issued timestamps.

nodes.summary: 90% of registrations happen within 48 hours of event announcement — registration form load time is critical in that window
nodes.details: Analysis by pm-lead: Data from existing EMC shows a sharp registration spike in the 48 hours after an event is announced via email blast. The registration form must handle burst traffic and load in under 2 seconds. This informed the decision to CDN-cache the form schema and pre-warm the registration API Lambda.

nodes.summary: React Spectrum 2 Tabs component can crash when overflow/collapse unmounts its internal TabListStateContext; use SegmentedControl + conditional rendering instead.
nodes.details: S2 horizontal Tabs on the Registrations page (/registrations) can enter an overflow/collapse path that unmounts the react-aria-components Tabs shell, leaving TabListStateContext null and causing 'Cannot read properties of null (reading selectedKey)' crashes. Replace with SegmentedControl + SegmentedControlItem (the established EMC pattern) paired with selectedTab state to conditionally render the three sections (Registrations, Campaigns, Sessions). This avoids the context unmounting issue entirely. See web-src/src/pages/Registrations/Registrations.tsx for the applied pattern.

nodes.summary: IMS user context must be threaded as a prop through component tree (App → UserPanel, SideBar); UserPanel displays profile data with graceful fallback when IMS profile unavailable.
nodes.details: The UserPanel component receives an `ims` prop containing `{ profile?: IMSProfile, org?: string, token?: string }` where IMSProfile has `userId`, `name`, `email`. Components extract user context via optional chaining (e.g., `ims.profile?.name || 'Guest'`). When `ims.profile` is absent, UserPanel renders 'Not Connected' state. This pattern establishes the contract for how IMS data flows through the EMC frontend: App.tsx passes `ims` to both UserPanel and SideBar, and any component needing user context receives the same IMS object structure. Token is never rendered; user ID is truncated in UI for privacy.

nodes.summary: EMC's per-option RSVP UI state model does not map cleanly to the event API's flat rsvpFormFields structure
nodes.details: The Event Management Console maintains granular per-option UI state for RSVP fields, while the underlying event API only exposes coarser visible/required flags on rsvpFormFields. This impedance mismatch requires a translation layer or dual-source loading strategy on the frontend. Future pods touching RSVP field configuration should budget time to handle this gap explicitly rather than assuming API parity.

nodes.summary: Event creation-to-publish time is the key organizer productivity metric — target under 15 minutes
nodes.details: Analysis by pm-lead: Tracking data from the existing EMC shows average event creation-to-publish time of 35 minutes. Most time is spent on session scheduling and RSVP form configuration. Reducing this to 15 minutes requires: (1) cloning from templates, (2) default configs at org level, (3) bulk session creation. These insights should inform the Sessions and Configs pods.

nodes.summary: EMC uses environment-specific Google Places API keys (DEV_/STAGE_/PROD_ prefixes) loaded from .env, with automatic selection based on runtime environment.
nodes.details: The application loads Google Places API via loadGooglePlacesAPI() utility in VenueComponent on mount. nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. nodes.summary: EMC migrated from sidebar to top navigation (gnav) layout; TopNav component in SideBar.tsx with UserPanel compact mode; App.tsx grid changed from ['sidebar', 'content'] to ['header', 'content'] with rows ['auto', '1fr'].
nodes.details: The layout shift encodes a durable architectural pattern: (1) SideBar.tsx was repurposed as TopNav with horizontal nav items and brand logo on left, user panel on right; (2) UserPanel.tsx gained a `compact` prop that hides email/org and reduces avatar size for header context; (3) App.tsx grid layout changed from 2-column sidebar model to 2-row header model with grid areas ['header', 'content'] and rows ['auto', '1fr']; (4) Navigation links use `.nav-link` class with bottom border (3px solid transparent) for active state, not background highlight; (5) Content area must have `gridArea='content'` and overflow scroll enabled. nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: Speakers and sponsors are grouped by role/tier with per-group drag-and-drop reordering; role/tier changes move items to the end of the new group and trigger per-group ordinal recomputation.

Both components display a disclaimer note that group display order on the DA page is governed by template configuration, not EMC form ordering.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: EMC dev token system uses two-path bootstrap architecture: ExC Shell path (real IMS) vs. standalone path (dev token), with dev token activation gated by both hostname allowlist AND ?devtokenmode=true URL parameter.
nodes.details: The dev token system is never active in Experience Cloud Shell (bootstrapInExcShell() path); it only activates in standalone mode (bootstrapStandalone()) when both hostname is in DEV_TOKEN_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES (localhost, 127.0.0.1, or specific adobeio-static.net subdomains) AND URL contains ?devtokenmode=true. The isDevTokenModeEnabled() function in web-src/src/config/env.ts enforces this dual gate. Dev token button visibility, token storage use in ApiService.getAuthToken(), and useDevToken hook all depend on this check. This ensures dev tokens never leak into production/staging deployments and cannot interfere with real IMS sessions in the shell.

nodes.summary: Dev token system is gated by both URL query parameter (?devtokenmode=true) and host allowlist (localhost or approved dev instances); without the parameter, the UI button is hidden and stored tokens are not used for API calls.
nodes.details: The dev token feature in EMC requires two conditions to be active: (1) the URL must include ?devtokenmode=true and (2) the host must be localhost or an approved dev instance (e.g., 14257-emc-dev.adobeio-static.net). When both conditions are met, the Dev Token button appears in the top-right UI and API calls use the stored token via tokenStorage.getValidToken(). When running in Adobe Experience Cloud Shell, the real IMS token is automatically used instead and the dev token button never appears. API calls should use constructRequestHeaders(token) and safeFetch() helpers to inject the token into request headers.

nodes.summary: EMC caching and throttling utilities follow a three-layer request pattern (cache → pending → new request) with function-name-based key generation, 10-second default TTL, pattern-based invalidation, and automatic cache busting on mutations.
nodes.details: The `apiCache` utility in `web-src/src/services/cacheUtils.ts` implements request deduplication and memoization via an IIFE module pattern. All GET operations in `cachedApi` (in `web-src/src/services/api.ts` ~line 1680+) are wrapped with `apiCache.get()`, and mutations automatically invalidate related cache entries by pattern matching (e.g., `cachedApi.updateEvent()` invalidates `getEvent()` and `getEventsList()` caches). URL-based caches use `fetchThrottledMemoizedText` and `fetchThrottledMemoizedJSON` with configurable TTL. Debounce (300ms for search) and throttle (100-200ms for scroll/resize) utilities follow the same patterns documented in `throttling.md`. Cache can be inspected via `getCacheStats()` and cleared via `clearCache()` or `invalidateCache(pattern)`.

nodes.summary: Claude agent access policy: read-only commands auto-approved, destructive operations require explicit approval; word-boundary matching prevents false positives in command filtering.
nodes.details: The EMC repo grants Claude agent file-edit permissions without prompting (defaultMode: acceptEdits) but enforces approval gates on destructive operations. Allowed commands (ls, cat, grep, find, echo, pwd, which) use word-boundary matching in Bash regex — e.g., Bash(ls *) matches 'ls -la' but not 'lsof', preventing accidental approval of unintended commands. Denied list includes rm -rf *, git push *, git reset --hard *, git merge *, and any --force flags. This pattern balances agent velocity (no friction on safe reads/edits) against repository safety (human-in-loop for irreversible changes).

nodes.summary: Silent failures in Splash attendee status updates (PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id) due to missing externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mappings caused EMC/Splash count mismatches; resolved via direct DynamoDB correction.
nodes.details: When Splash sends status updates via PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id without a valid externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mapping in the service layer, the request fails silently rather than returning an error, leaving EMC counts stale while Splash reflects the true state. This caused deltas of 135+ waitlisted and 80+ declined records. Future agents should: (1) audit the attendee mapping lookup logic in the PUT handler to ensure it returns explicit errors on missing mappings rather than silently skipping updates, (2) add monitoring/alerting on PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id response codes to catch similar silent failures early, (3) recognize that zzTest migration scripts in this repo are the canonical runbook for data reconciliation when such mismatches occur.

nodes.summary: event-libs exports a consolidated entry point (libs.js) that re-exports utilities from six internal modules, enabling single-import consumption instead of Promise.all() across multiple paths.
nodes.details: Consumers should import from `${EVENT_LIBS}/libs.js` rather than individually importing from utils.js, decorate.js, profile.js, dictionary-manager.js, esp-controller.js, and data-utils.js. The consolidated module re-exports all public utilities (setEventConfig, decorateEvent, getNonProdData, validatePageAndRedirect, lazyCaptureProfile, dictionaryManager, getProfile, getEvent, getEventAttendee, etc.) plus the EVENT_BLOCKS constant for block discovery. This pattern maintains tree-shaking compatibility while reducing import boilerplate and centralizing the public API surface.

nodes.summary: RichTextEditor export must use getSemanticHTML() to produce portable <ul>/<ol> instead of Quill's internal data-list markup; normalize NBSP variants on load/export for API consistency.
nodes.details: In web-src/src/components/shared/RichTextEditor.tsx, call getSemanticHTML() instead of root.innerHTML when exporting editor content so that bullet lists serialize as semantic <ul> and numbered lists as <ol>, not Quill 2's internal <ol data-list="…"> format. This ensures stored HTML is portable across APIs and event copy systems. Additionally, normalize all NBSP variants ( ,  , \u00A0) to regular spaces during both load (via clipboard.convert + setContents) and export, and align onChange / prop sync comparisons on the normalized form to prevent re-apply loops and caret jumps. Restrict formats whitelist to toolbar capabilities (bold, italic, underline, strike, list, indent, align, link) to prevent pasted content from retaining unwanted styling (color, background, font, size).

This centralizes read-only-field stripping and ensures unpublish, archive, and external-update flows all go through the same validation layer. Do not invent ad-hoc filtering at the call site.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: EMC dev token system uses two-path bootstrap architecture: ExC Shell path (real IMS) vs. standalone path (dev token), with dev token activation gated by both hostname allowlist AND ?devtokenmode=true URL parameter.
nodes.details: The dev token system is never active in Experience Cloud Shell (bootstrapInExcShell() path); it only activates in standalone mode (bootstrapStandalone()) when both hostname is in DEV_TOKEN_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES (localhost, 127.0.0.1, or specific adobeio-static.net subdomains) AND URL contains ?devtokenmode=true. The isDevTokenModeEnabled() function in web-src/src/config/env.ts enforces this dual gate. Dev token button visibility, token storage use in ApiService.getAuthToken(), and useDevToken hook all depend on this check. This ensures dev tokens never leak into production/staging deployments and cannot interfere with real IMS sessions in the shell.

nodes.summary: Session-time helpers must return SessionTimeInfo so React state can update without a page refresh
nodes.details: createSessionTimeForSession and upsertSessionTimeForSession previously returned Promise<void>, which dropped the API's sessionTimeId, creationTime, and modificationTime on the floor. Calling components could not update local state with the new optimistic-concurrency values, so users saw stale data and had to refresh the page after every session-time edit. Fix is to return the API response from both helpers and have handleAddSession / handleUpdateSession capture and propagate sessionTimeId + creationTime + modificationTime into local React session state. This is the EMC-wide convention for any API helper that yields server-issued timestamps.

nodes.summary: Dev token system is gated by both URL query parameter (?devtokenmode=true) and host allowlist (localhost or approved dev instances); without the parameter, the UI button is hidden and stored tokens are not used for API calls.
nodes.details: The dev token feature in EMC requires two conditions to be active: (1) the URL must include ?devtokenmode=true and (2) the host must be localhost or an approved dev instance (e.g., 14257-emc-dev.adobeio-static.net). When both conditions are met, the Dev Token button appears in the top-right UI and API calls use the stored token via tokenStorage.getValidToken(). When running in Adobe Experience Cloud Shell, the real IMS token is automatically used instead and the dev token button never appears. API calls should use constructRequestHeaders(token) and safeFetch() helpers to inject the token into request headers.

nodes.summary: EMC migrated from sidebar to top navigation (gnav) layout; TopNav component in SideBar.tsx with UserPanel compact mode; App.tsx grid changed from ['sidebar', 'content'] to ['header', 'content'] with rows ['auto', '1fr'].
nodes.details: The layout shift encodes a durable architectural pattern: (1) SideBar.tsx was repurposed as TopNav with horizontal nav items and brand logo on left, user panel on right; (2) UserPanel.tsx gained a `compact` prop that hides email/org and reduces avatar size for header context; (3) App.tsx grid layout changed from 2-column sidebar model to 2-row header model with grid areas ['header', 'content'] and rows ['auto', '1fr']; (4) Navigation links use `.nav-link` class with bottom border (3px solid transparent) for active state, not background highlight; (5) Content area must have `gridArea='content'` and overflow scroll enabled. nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). nodes.summary: IMS user context must be threaded as a prop through component tree (App → UserPanel, SideBar); UserPanel displays profile data with graceful fallback when IMS profile unavailable.
nodes.details: The UserPanel component receives an `ims` prop containing `{ profile?: IMSProfile, org?: string, token?: string }` where IMSProfile has `userId`, `name`, `email`. Components extract user context via optional chaining (e.g., `ims.profile?.name || 'Guest'`). When `ims.profile` is absent, UserPanel renders 'Not Connected' state. This pattern establishes the contract for how IMS data flows through the EMC frontend: App.tsx passes `ims` to both UserPanel and SideBar, and any component needing user context receives the same IMS object structure. Token is never rendered; user ID is truncated in UI for privacy.

nodes.summary: Event creation-to-publish time is the key organizer productivity metric — target under 15 minutes
nodes.details: Analysis by pm-lead: Tracking data from the existing EMC shows average event creation-to-publish time of 35 minutes. Most time is spent on session scheduling and RSVP form configuration. Reducing this to 15 minutes requires: (1) cloning from templates, (2) default configs at org level, (3) bulk session creation. These insights should inform the Sessions and Configs pods.

nodes.summary: EMC App Builder development uses Experience Cloud Shell devMode with deployed backend + local frontend hot reload for IMS-authenticated development; backend changes require `aio app deploy --actions` redeploy.
nodes.details: The recommended development workflow is: (1) deploy backend actions once via `aio app deploy`, (2) access frontend via `https://experience.adobe.com/?devMode=true#/@ORG/APP-ID` which enables hot reload of `web-src/` changes and automatic IMS token injection, (3) for backend changes, redeploy via `aio app deploy --actions`. The app.config.yaml annotation `require-adobe-auth: true` ensures Adobe API Gateway validates IMS tokens before actions execute. Frontend receives IMS data via `runtime.on('ready', ({ imsOrg, imsToken, imsProfile }))` and must pass tokens in API calls; developers should never manually manage tokens. Local-only mode (`aio app run --local`) is for action debugging only, not production-like IMS testing.

nodes.summary: Scope-level configs (locales, rsvp, custom-attributes) are consolidated into a single typed config system with full-replace hierarchy merge per type, replacing publishing profiles and hardcoded locales.
nodes.details: Configs are stored per scope (org/team only, not platform) with one config per type. Hierarchy merge is full-replace: if a team scope has a config of the same type as its parent org, the team's config completely replaces the parent's (not a partial merge). Custom attributes are NOT a separate entity—they are consolidated as `type: 'custom-attributes'` within the config system. Event custom attribute values are denormalized into the event's `itemData.customAttributes` array as `[{ attributeId, attribute, valueId, value, displayOrder }, ...]`. Backend manager methods: `createScopeConfig`, `getScopeConfigWithLocalizations`, `listConfigsForScope`, `updateScopeConfig`, `deleteScopeConfig` in `src/managers/scopesMgr.js`. Routes use `requirePermission('config', 'read/write/delete')`. DynamoDB stores config records with pk `config#<configId>`, localizations in separate row with sk `localizations`. Locales migration: `GET /v1/locales` deprecated in favor of `GET /v1/series/{seriesId}/configs?type=locales`; hardcoded fallback remains. Publishing profiles marked deprecated in OpenAPI but not removed.

nodes.summary: Silent failures in Splash attendee status updates (PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id) due to missing externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mappings caused EMC/Splash count mismatches; resolved via direct DynamoDB correction.
nodes.details: When Splash sends status updates via PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id without a valid externalAttendeeId → attendeeId mapping in the service layer, the request fails silently rather than returning an error, leaving EMC counts stale while Splash reflects the true state. This caused deltas of 135+ waitlisted and 80+ declined records. Future agents should: (1) audit the attendee mapping lookup logic in the PUT handler to ensure it returns explicit errors on missing mappings rather than silently skipping updates, (2) add monitoring/alerting on PUT /external/events/:id/attendees/:id response codes to catch similar silent failures early, (3) recognize that zzTest migration scripts in this repo are the canonical runbook for data reconciliation when such mismatches occur.

nodes.summary: Consent suite visibility and country-region capture follow a locale-aware, metadata-driven pattern: force-consent-collection metadata controls suite visibility; country picker data-country-code maps to payload.countryRegion; consent index URL uses locale-prefixed fallback pattern matching promotional-content.
nodes.details: In events-form.js, the consent suite (country picker + terms) is conditionally rendered based on user type (guest) OR force-consent-collection metadata being true. Country pre-selection logic runs whenever the suite is present. The consent query index JSON is fetched via getConsentQueryIndexUrl() using getLocale() + FALLBACK_LOCALES pattern (same as promotional-content), not a static URL. On form submit, the selected country option's data-country-code attribute is extracted and sent as payload.countryRegion in the baseAttendee object; BASE_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER already whitelists this field. This establishes the contract: force-consent-collection is a boolean metadata flag that overrides guest-only consent visibility, and country selection always populates countryRegion when the suite is shown.

nodes.summary: Claude agent access policy: read-only commands auto-approved, destructive operations require explicit approval; word-boundary matching prevents false positives in command filtering.
nodes.details: The EMC repo grants Claude agent file-edit permissions without prompting (defaultMode: acceptEdits) but enforces approval gates on destructive operations. Allowed commands (ls, cat, grep, find, echo, pwd, which) use word-boundary matching in Bash regex — e.g., Bash(ls *) matches 'ls -la' but not 'lsof', preventing accidental approval of unintended commands. Denied list includes rm -rf *, git push *, git reset --hard *, git merge *, and any --force flags. This pattern balances agent velocity (no friction on safe reads/edits) against repository safety (human-in-loop for irreversible changes).

nodes.summary: Speaker photo hydration requires explicit imagesMgr.list() join; photos are stored as separate DynamoDB records (sk: imagekind#speaker-photo) and must be fetched and attached to speaker objects.
nodes.details: In src/routes/events/speakers/read.js, both GET /v1/events/:eventId/speakers (list) and GET /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId (single) endpoints must call imagesMgr.list() in parallel and join photo records onto speaker objects by matching speaker ID. This pattern is already correctly implemented in GET /v1/series/:seriesId/speakers and should be mirrored across all speaker-returning endpoints. Speakers without uploaded photos should return without a photo field (not null or error). Omitting this hydration step leaves the photo field missing from the response contract.

nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Tokens are duplicated under html[data-color-scheme='dark'] selector to ensure first paint and post-effect hydration alignment. Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.

nodes.summary: ESP resources use modificationTime for optimistic concurrency on PUT; clients must round-trip it
nodes.details: Every ESP PUT on an updatable resource (event, series, session, speaker) requires the modificationTime field to match the server's last-known value. If they differ, PUT returns 409 with the current server state. Clients must therefore: (a) capture modificationTime on every GET, (b) send it back unchanged on the next PUT, (c) re-fetch on 409 and merge. Dropping or recomputing modificationTime client-side is the most common cause of silent edit failures on EMC.

nodes.summary: EMC App Builder development uses Experience Cloud Shell devMode with deployed backend + local frontend hot reload for IMS-authenticated development; backend changes require `aio app deploy --actions` redeploy.
