nodes.summary: Scope configs (rsvp, locales, customAttributes) are the authoritative source for event metadata; publishing profiles are deprecated but retained for backward compatibility during migration.
nodes.details: Events created under Creative Events (25f26faa-f8e2-4e99-b341-81a3995ef9af) and Enterprise Events (d758a3bc-ff31-4bfe-a2f5-343f074aec6c) scopes must define four config types: rsvp (pool of form fields), locales (localeNames, localeUrlCodes), and customAttributes (with primaryProductName and promotionalItems attributes). The Kinesis processor (events-kinesis-processor/ServiceProcessor.applyRelatedData) must call GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs to hydrate event.locales, event.customAttributesConfig, and event.rsvpConfig at stream-processing time; event DDB records store only user selections (rsvpFormFields, customAttributes[] with valueId), not full definitions. Publishing profiles remain in the payload for backward compat but are no longer the source of truth. hoolihan-webhooks must read primary product from event.customAttributes[] where attribute='primaryProductName', promotional items from customAttributes[] where attribute='promotionalItems', RSVP pool from event.rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields[], and locales from event.locales.localeNames/localeUrlCodes.

nodes.summary: RSVP form field configuration requires option-level granularity (subset selection, ordering) that is non-trivial on the BE and easy to underestimate
nodes.details: The assumption that rsvpFormFields could be manipulated at the field level was insufficient — option-level control (enabling/disabling individual options, reordering them) required separate, unplanned BE work. Any pod touching RSVP or dynamic form-field configuration should scope BE option-level support as an explicit, separate work item.

nodes.summary: Event creation-to-publish time is the key organizer productivity metric — target under 15 minutes
nodes.details: Analysis by pm-lead: Tracking data from the existing EMC shows average event creation-to-publish time of 35 minutes. Most time is spent on session scheduling and RSVP form configuration. Reducing this to 15 minutes requires: (1) cloning from templates, (2) default configs at org level, (3) bulk session creation. These insights should inform the Sessions and Configs pods.

nodes.summary: Scope configs unify RSVP forms, locales, and custom attributes under a single typed config system with scope-inherited hierarchy (org → team) and full-replace merge semantics.
nodes.details: All configuration for the events console — RSVP form fields, locale definitions, and custom attribute definitions — is managed through a single `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs` API with `type` field (e.g., 'rsvp', 'locales', 'custom-attributes'). Configs inherit down the scope hierarchy with full-replace merge per type. Frontend reads merged configs via `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs` or `GET /v1/series/{seriesId}/configs` with optional `?type=` filter. Custom attributes are a config type, not a separate entity. Admin management uses POST/PUT/DELETE on `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs/{configId}` and requires `config:read`, `config:write`, or `config:delete` permissions.

nodes.summary: Registration form preview mode renders the form with sample data without creating records — essential for organizer testing
nodes.details: Implemented by fe-agent-registration: The RSVP form editor includes a 'Preview' button that renders the FormRenderer in read-only mode with sample data. The preview uses the same rendering path as the live form but submits to a no-op endpoint. This lets organizers see exactly how their form will look before publishing, including locale overlays and custom attributes.

nodes.summary: RSVP field option panels render inline within the field card with conditional icon toggle; drag interactions collapse all open panels to enforce mutual exclusivity.
nodes.details: In RegistrationFieldsComponent.tsx, option panels for RSVP fields (select, multi-select) now render as children inside the field card border rather than as sibling elements below. The expand/collapse trigger is a ListBulleted icon in a 5th grid column (only rendered for fields with selectable options via rsvpFieldDefinitions.ts). The icon highlights in selection-ring color when open. Starting a field drag operation collapses all open option panels—this is a deliberate UX constraint to prevent simultaneous drag and panel interactions. Option rows no longer have individual borders; drag-over ring feedback is retained. Fields without options have no list icon and no extra column gap.

nodes.summary: Scope configs support optional admin-set `label` field; UI falls back to `humanReadableType(type)` when label is absent, with raw type shown as muted secondary text.
nodes.details: The `label` field is optional in `Config` and `ConfigCreateBody` OpenAPI schemas. Frontend renders `label ?? humanReadableType(type)` in the configs table (label in bold, type as muted secondary). The `humanReadableType()` helper converts camelCase type names to title case (e.g., `rsvp` → RSVP, `customAttributes` → Custom Attributes). Label is added to `SYSTEM_KEYS` to prevent KeyValueEditor from surfacing it as a raw field. Both Create and Edit modals include a Label TextField; Create omits it from payload if blank. Custom attribute items also support a label field between Name and Type rows in CustomAttributesEditor.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events gate RSVP behind `inviteOnly` flag and campaign URL param; replace button with text message rather than disable.
nodes.details: The invite-only RSVP feature gates registration on two conditions: (1) an `inviteOnly` event flag from the backend, and (2) a campaign URL parameter. When both conditions are met, the RSVP button is replaced with a text message instead of being disabled. This pattern prevents accidental user confusion and clarifies that the event is not available for self-service registration. Check `event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js` for the gating logic and button replacement implementation.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.
nodes.details: When submitting event-attendee payloads for RSVP, include `requiresSxswTicket` boolean when SXSW ticket filter applies (#140). Implicit consent for new registrations is recorded via the `contactMethods` field in the payload (MWPW-194036, #126). In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.summary: Localization overlays on RSVP forms: base field definitions + per-locale label/placeholder overrides
nodes.details: Implemented by fe-agent-registration: The RSVP form schema has a base layer (field types, ordering, validation rules) and per-locale overlays that override only label and placeholder strings. The FormRenderer selects the overlay matching the user's locale, falling back to the base layer. This keeps form structure consistent across locales while allowing full translation of user-facing text.

nodes.summary: ESL attendee schemas must stay synchronized with ESP spec; use generic field names (requiresTicket) at ESL layer even when ESP uses domain-specific names (requiresSxswTicket).
nodes.details: When ESP (events-service-platform) adds a new attendee field, ESL (events-service-layer) must mirror it in both EventAttendeeBody (request schema in src/api/openapi.json) and EventAttendee (response schema). ESL renames domain-specific ESP fields to generic names for reusability—e.g., ESP's requiresSxswTicket becomes requiresTicket at ESL. Since ESL passes attendee bodies directly through to ESP without transformation, the schema addition alone is sufficient; no transformer logic is required. Bump the OpenAPI spec version when adding fields.

nodes.summary: Attendee API field `requiresTicket` is the canonical name; prior `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed across routes, manager, and OpenAPI spec as part of generalization.
nodes.details: The field `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed to `requiresTicket` on `EventAttendeeBody` and `EventAttendee` schemas (MWPW-194794, PRs #954–#958). This change propagated through: (1) OpenAPI spec in `src/api/openapi.json`, (2) attendee manager in `src/managers/attendeesMgr.js`, and (3) all attendee routes (`src/routes/events/attendees/{create,read,update}.js`). The rename signals a shift from event-specific (SXSW) to generic event semantics. Future attendee schema changes should use `requiresTicket` as the canonical field name.

nodes.summary: Do not include event-specific fields (like requiresTicket) in BaseAttendee schema; they belong only on EventAttendeeBody and EventAttendee.
nodes.details: BaseAttendee is a shared schema for general attendee data across contexts. Event-specific constraints like requiresTicket must live only on EventAttendeeBody and EventAttendee schemas in src/api/openapi.json. This separation ensures that attendee data reused in non-event contexts doesn't carry event-specific validation rules. When refactoring field names (e.g., requiresSxswTicket → requiresTicket), verify the field's scope before placement in the schema hierarchy.

nodes.summary: Event-attendee payload fields must be explicitly listed in EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER to be sent to ESL's addAttendeeToEvent endpoint.
nodes.details: The EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in event-libs/v1/utils/data-utils.js acts as an allowlist for which form fields are included in the event-attendee payload sent to ESL. New checkbox or form fields (e.g., requiresSxswTicket, shareInfoWithPartners) must be added to this filter in getEventAttendeePayload() to be transmitted. Additionally, when gating form fields via rsvp-form-fields metadata in events-form.js, new sheet fields must be listed in the visible array to render; unlisted fields are silently dropped.

nodes.summary: The `requiresTicket` field must be explicitly mapped in attendeeMap and included in listAttendeesForEvent push operations to appear in GET /events/{eventId}/attendees responses.
nodes.details: In src/managers/attendeesMgr.js, the `listAttendeesForEvent` function builds an `attendeeMap` object and pushes attendee records to `result.attendees`. The `requiresTicket` field must be explicitly included in both the map construction and the push payload; it does not automatically propagate from the database layer. This pattern applies to all attendee response fields—verify each field is present in the attendeeMap and result.attendees.push call, not just in create/update/read handlers.

nodes.summary: requiresSxswTicket is stored on attendee records but intentionally does not sync to Splash; form availability is gated at console level, not API level.
nodes.details: The requiresSxswTicket field (boolean, optional) is added to BaseAttendee, EventAttendeeBody, and EventAttendee schemas in src/api/openapi.json. It is accepted and stored as-is on attendee records via POST events/{eventId}/attendees and POST attendees endpoints, and returned in GET responses. Critically, this field is NOT included in Splash custom field mappings — it remains local to the events platform. Field visibility/requirement is controlled by Event Marketers at the console level (not API-enforced), meaning the API accepts the field regardless of event cloud-type. This establishes the boundary: events-service-platform owns storage and retrieval; console owns form presentation logic; Splash integration is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.summary: RSVP field metadata is loaded from external event-libs config via configService.getRsvpConfig; boolean attendee fields render as 'Yes'/'No' in UI and CSV exports.
nodes.details: RegistrationFieldsComponent loads RSVP field catalogs via configService.getRsvpConfig (with caching/retry), and renders each field's Label from the JSON config. In AttendeeTableComponent, boolean columns (e.g., requiresSxswTicket) display as 'yes'/'no' in table cells; AttendeeFiltersComponent maps filter chips to 'Yes'/'No'; ExportDialog normalizes boolean columns to 'Yes'/'No' in CSV. The field definition lives in external event-libs experiencecloud.json (not in EMC repo), following the Type/Options conventions of other Experience Cloud RSVP fields. Add requiresSxswTicket?: boolean to attendee.ts type definitions.

nodes.summary: Adding fields to base schemas without confirming they apply universally causes downstream churn
nodes.details: requiresTicket was placed in BaseAttendee before its domain scope was validated, requiring two follow-up spec changes to move it to the correct event-specific types. Placing fields in base/shared schemas prematurely inflates the contract and forces breaking changes. Future pods should default to the most specific schema location and promote upward only when generality is confirmed.

nodes.summary: Spec-implementation gaps on persisted fields (e.g. requiresTicket not written to or returned from DynamoDB) can survive initial review and require dedicated closure work
nodes.details: requiresTicket was present in the schema but not being persisted to DynamoDB or included in GET responses until an explicit gap-closure change was made. This suggests field lifecycle (define → persist → return) is not always completed atomically. Future pods should include a checklist step confirming each new schema field is handled at all persistence and retrieval points.

nodes.summary: Event attendee route handlers use explicit field mappings instead of spreading req.body, causing OpenAPI-validated fields to silently drop before persistence.
nodes.details: The attendee CRUD routes (create.js, update.js, read.js) in src/routes/events/attendees/ build eventAttendee objects by hand-picking fields rather than spreading req.body. This means fields validated by the OpenAPI spec (e.g., requiresTicket) can pass validation but never reach DynamoDB or the response. When adding a new attendee field, it must be explicitly added to all three route handlers' field mappings, or it will be silently dropped. Use explicit field mappings only when you need to exclude or transform fields; otherwise, spread req.body and filter at the schema layer.

nodes.summary: Field placement in schema hierarchies requires upfront domain modeling to avoid rename/revert cycles
nodes.details: The requiresTicket field was added to BaseAttendee, then removed and relocated to event-specific types after recognizing it was event-scoped rather than universal. Similarly, ordinal was renamed to displayOrder and then reverted. These churn cycles suggest schema field ownership (base vs. domain-specific type) was not resolved before implementation began. Future pods should explicitly map field scope to schema layer before committing field names.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.
nodes.details: When submitting event-attendee payloads for RSVP, include `requiresSxswTicket` boolean when SXSW ticket filter applies (#140). Implicit consent for new registrations is recorded via the `contactMethods` field in the payload (MWPW-194036, #126). In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.summary: ESL must mirror ESP's AttendeeTextField relaxations (maxLength 100→200, newline-tolerant regex) to avoid being a stricter validation gate than upstream, preventing legacy attendee data from passing re-validation.
nodes.details: When ESL re-validates attendee payloads against its own OpenAPI spec, fields like `invitedBy` and `campaignId` (both typed as `AttendeeTextField`) must accept the same input that ESP accepts. The original pattern `^(?!.*<[^>]*>).*$` rejected newlines; the relaxed pattern `^(?![\s\S]*<[^>]*>)[\s\S]*$` accepts them. maxLength was raised from 100 to 200 characters. This is not a feature expansion—it is a compatibility fix to unblock legacy data that ESP already accepts. Do not selectively port only some field relaxations from ESP; ESL's `BaseAttendee` / `EventAttendee` schemas define which fields exist, and only those should be relaxed (e.g., `PhoneNumber` is unreferenced in ESL and should not be changed).

nodes.summary: EMC is a frontend-only ExC Shell SPA with no backend repo; all mutations and queries call external Adobe APIs (ESP, ESL) directly through a centralized ApiService with caching, validation, and dry-run support.
nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: AttendeeTextField maxLength relaxed from 100 to 200 chars to prevent ESL from being a stricter validation gate than upstream ESP for invitedBy and campaignId fields.
nodes.details: ESP encountered PROD failures when legacy attendee records exceeded the 100-char cap on AttendeeTextField in GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees responses. ESL's POST /events/{eventId}/attendees/{attendeeId} validates invitedBy and campaignId via the same AttendeeTextField schema ($ref in openapi.json:2006). To maintain schema alignment and prevent ESL from rejecting valid payloads that ESP accepts, maxLength was bumped to 200. The injection pattern (^(?!.*<[^>]*>).*$) remains unchanged. PhoneNumber and mobilePhone/businessPhone fields were not ported because they have zero $refs in ESL's spec.

nodes.summary: Do not spread oldData wholesale into validation or payload comparisons; explicitly whitelist keys to avoid introducing undocumented OpenAPI spec changes.
nodes.details: When comparing or processing oldData in EventDataStreamProcessor.js, explicitly check for specific keys (e.g., hostEmail) rather than iterating over the entire oldData object. This prevents accidental introduction of unknown fields into the OpenAPI spec (src/api/openapi.json). The pattern applies to Kinesis event processors where oldData is used for change detection or payload construction—always use an allowlist of known fields to maintain spec alignment with ESL (events-service-layer).

nodes.summary: When hydrating event payloads from DynamoDB kinesis records with sk=localizations, source seriesId and detailPagePath from the pre-fetched liveData object, not from newData.itemData (which lacks these fields).
nodes.details: In EventDataStreamProcessor.js, when processing a localization record change (sk=localizations), the newData.itemData payload contains only localizations and localizationOverrides. To build a complete hydrated event for ESL, pull seriesId and detailPagePath from liveData (fetched via eventService.getEventData at processRecord start), not from newData.itemData. This is safe because EventService.updateVenue writes the new detailPagePath to DynamoDB before the venue record fires the kinesis stream, ensuring liveData.detailPagePath is current. Omitting these fields causes DA webhook page creation to fail or write to wrong locations.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The fix: in useEventFormSave.ts, call dataFilters to set detailPagePath.submittable = true before the PUT, and detect title changes to trigger the DA page path dialog. This requires coordinated backend changes to the OpenAPI spec to allow the field in PUT requests. The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: Attendee string fields are validated via reusable OpenAPI schemas (NoTagsString, AttendeeName, AttendeeTextField, SpecialRequirements, PhoneNumber) enforced by express-openapi-validator at the API layer to prevent injection attacks and enforce length limits.
nodes.details: All attendee string inputs must pass schema validation in src/api/openapi.json before reaching business logic. NoTagsString rejects values containing `<…>` (HTML/script tags). AttendeeName (firstName, lastName) max 30 chars; AttendeeTextField (companyName, countryRegion, organizationName, title, dietaryRestrictions, etc.) max 100 chars; SpecialRequirements max 1000 chars; PhoneNumber (mobilePhone, businessPhone) digits + `+` only, max 20 chars. Website (format: uri) and executiveAssistantEmail (format: email) use existing OpenAPI format constraints; contactMethod uses enum. Validation is declarative in openapi.json and enforced by express-openapi-validator middleware — do not add runtime validation in handlers.

nodes.summary: ESP owns session/event/series/cloud entities and their integrations; Rainfocus scheduler is a separate ingest layer that transforms RF data into ESP schema via ESL API.
nodes.details: The architecture establishes clear ownership: ESP (via ESL API) owns the DynamoDB Events Table (sessions, events, series, clouds, integrations); the events-scheduler Lambda is a separate ingest component that pulls from Rainfocus, transforms via RainfocusDataProcessor, and writes via POST/PUT /api/v1/sessions/{id}. The integration layer (events-integration-processor) consumes DynamoDB Kinesis streams and executes integrations scoped to session/event/series/cloud. This means: (1) ESP does not own Rainfocus polling logic, (2) integrations are defined per entity scope and triggered by DynamoDB change events, (3) the scheduler is stateless except for optional S3 config (lastRunTimestamp).

nodes.summary: Kinesis event processor compares old and new records to send only modified attributes to webhooks, reducing payload size while maintaining backward compatibility for localization fallbacks.
nodes.details: The EventDataStreamProcessor and ServiceProcessor in aws/templates/lambda/events-kinesis-processor/ implement a delta-detection pattern: before forwarding events to ESL and webhooks, compare the incoming Kinesis record against the previous state and transmit only changed fields. This applies uniformly to localizations, localizationOverrides, and top-level attributes. Maintain backward compatibility by falling back to top-level attributes when localizationOverrides or localizations for a given locale are absent. This reduces webhook payload size while ensuring consumers receive complete, usable data.

nodes.summary: Carousel late-loading uses `is-delayed` class with `requestAnimationFrame` to prevent layout shift on initial render; consumers must apply this class and let carousel remove it after first paint.
nodes.details: The `milo-carousel` component implements a late-loading pattern via `is-delayed` CSS class and `requestAnimationFrame` in milo-carousel.js to defer carousel initialization until after the first browser paint, preventing layout thrashing. Consumers (profile-cards, bento-cards) must apply `is-delayed` to the carousel container; the component removes it once mounted. This pattern is critical for avoiding Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) on pages with multiple carousels. The CSS hides carousel controls while `is-delayed` is present, and JS removes the class after rAF callback completes.

nodes.summary: Detect session description truncation via DOM layout (scrollHeight vs clientHeight) rather than character limits; re-sync on filter, expand/collapse, font load, and resize events.
nodes.details: In sessions-hub.js, replace fixed-character truncation logic with dynamic overflow detection: compare element.scrollHeight > element.clientHeight to determine if text is truncated. Export syncSessionDescriptionsOverflow() and call it after filter changes, expand/collapse toggles, fonts ready (via document.fonts.ready), and ResizeObserver triggers. This ensures descriptions adapt to actual layout constraints (viewport, font metrics, container width) rather than hardcoded thresholds. Apply the same sync pattern to the conflict modal: defer modal close until registration completes, show pending state on confirm button and option elements, and restore UI on failure.

nodes.summary: profile-cards block supports a `modal` variant that renders full profile content in a Milo modal on card interaction, with hover elevation styling and responsive image constraints (max 385px width).
nodes.details: The profile-cards block in event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/ now accepts a `modal` variant class that triggers Milo modal rendering for profile details. The variant applies hover elevation styling via CSS and enforces a 385px maximum width constraint on modal images. This pattern applies to both metadata-driven cards (from ESP) and static-authored cards, maintaining responsive behavior across viewport sizes. Implementation spans profile-cards.js (modal trigger logic), profile-cards.css (elevation + image constraints), and corresponding test fixtures.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Tokens are duplicated under html[data-color-scheme='dark'] selector to ensure first paint and post-effect hydration alignment. Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on :focus:not(:focus-visible) CSS to suppress focus rings when Milo's getModal uses .focus({ focusVisible: true }) — the flag forces :focus-visible to match regardless of input method.
nodes.details: Milo's getModal helper focuses the first FOCUSABLE element using .focus({ focusVisible: true }), which explicitly forces :focus-visible to match even on programmatic focus. CSS rules like :focus:not(:focus-visible) cannot suppress this ring. Instead, ensure the first FOCUSABLE in modal DOM order is an element where outline: none is already applied (e.g., a heading with tabindex="0"), or add outline: none to the element that will receive initial focus. In profile-cards/profile-cards.js, the fix was to add tabindex="0" to the card-name h2 in buildModalContent so it precedes social links in focus order, and the existing .card-name:focus { outline: none; } rule suppresses the ring.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events without a valid campaign parameter must block RSVP UI and show a shared dictionary-driven message across all event blocks (decorate, events-form, sessions-hub).
nodes.details: When an invite-only event is opened without a valid `campaign` URL parameter, the RSVP flow is blocked. Use `dictionaryManager.getInviteOnlyNoCampaignMessage()` to fetch the user-facing message from the dictionary sheet. In sessions-hub, compute `inviteOnlyBlocked` after `await dictionaryManager.initialize()`, then replace the sticky Register CTA and per-card event-registration buttons with the status message. Guard all click handlers and sessionStorage-deferred modal opens to prevent RSVP submission. Apply CSS classes `.sh-banner-invite-only-msg` and `.sh-invite-only-msg` for styling. This pattern ensures parity across decorate.js, events-form.js, and sessions-hub.js.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend uses centralized design tokens (LAYOUT_DIMENSIONS, COLORS, Z_INDEX, pre-composed style objects) imported from `/web-src/src/styles/designSystem.ts` to enforce UI consistency and maintainability.
nodes.details: All layout dimensions (GNAV_HEIGHT=56px, ACTION_BAR_HEIGHT=60px, SIDE_NAV_WIDTH=240px), colors (COLORS.ADOBE_RED, COLORS.GRAY_*), z-index layering (Z_INDEX.MODAL=600, Z_INDEX.GNAV=1000), and common style patterns (STICKY_GNAV_STYLES, FIXED_ACTION_BAR_STYLES, SCROLLABLE_CONTENT_STYLES) must be imported from designSystem.ts rather than hardcoded. Helper functions like createFixedHeightStyle() and createActionBarPadding() compute viewport-relative dimensions. Button state colors (BUTTON_HOVER_OVERLAY, BUTTON_ACTIVE_OVERLAY) are defined but legacy—Spectrum defaults are preferred. This centralizes all UI constants and prevents drift across components.

nodes.summary: Sessions Hub text search is scoped to title, speaker names, and tag labels; descriptions excluded by default unless `search-include-description` block class is set.
nodes.details: The filterSessions function in event-libs/v1/blocks/sessions-hub/sessions-hub.js implements a three-field search pattern: title, speaker (first/last/full-name substring), and tag labels are matched case-insensitively against trimmed queries ≥2 characters. Session descriptions are intentionally excluded from the default search scope to reduce noise; marketers can opt into description matching by adding the `search-include-description` block class. A query of 1 character or whitespace-only does not filter by text, leaving all sessions visible subject to tab/tag filters. When a qualifying search returns zero results, the no-results UI (role="status", aria-live="polite") is shown and the session grid is hidden.

nodes.summary: Session location-time conflict validation must occur on both FE (inline UX + cost reduction) and BE (atomicity guard), with FE checking interval overlap via UTC millisecond conversion and BE as final arbiter.
nodes.details: SessionForm.tsx implements FE-side conflict detection by accepting allSessions prop, deriving hasLocationConflict via useMemo that converts form date/time to UTC milliseconds (reusing naiveDateTimeToUTCMillis + dateAndTimeToISO utilities) and scans for overlapping intervals on same locationId (currentStart < sEnd && currentEnd > sStart), excluding self in edit mode. This marks Location ComboBox isInvalid and blocks Save button. BE (events-service-platform PR #922) performs final DynamoDB scan validation. FE guard reduces unnecessary requests and narrows race-condition window; BE guard ensures atomicity. SessionsList threads allSessions through component hierarchy (SessionsListProps → SessionItemProps → SessionForm) for both add and edit forms; Sessions.tsx sources from existing state, no new fetches.

nodes.summary: Sessions tab in Event Report uses lazy-loaded expandable rows to display per-session attendee lists, cross-referencing session-time attendees with event attendees for display names.
nodes.details: The Sessions registration tab (SessionsTab.tsx) implements a table with expandable rows that lazy-load attendee data via getSessionTimeAttendees(timeId) from GET /v1/session-times/{timeId}/attendees. Attendee display names are resolved by cross-referencing the session-time attendee list against the parent event's attendee roster. SessionTimeInfo type extends with attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount, isFull fields. Expanded state resets when switching events to avoid stale data.

nodes.summary: Profile card heading hierarchy and typography must align with Figma design specs: card names render as h2 (not h3), descriptions use Body/L (18px/27px), and modal focus outlines are suppressed.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/, all render paths (decorateContent, decorateContentSimple, buildModalContent) must output card names as `<h2>` elements, not h3. Card description text (`.card-desc`) must use CSS custom properties `--type-body-l-size` and `--type-body-l-lh` (18px/27px) instead of `--type-body-xs-size` (14px/21px). Section heading h2 selectors must be scoped to `.profile-cards > div:first-child h2` to prevent style bleed to card-level h2s. Modal overlays must suppress the browser default focus outline on `.profile-cards-modal .card-name` with `outline: none;` to match Figma design intent. These constraints apply to both card view and modal render modes.

nodes.summary: RSVP form `limit` field is applied only to text inputs and textareas via HTML `maxlength` attribute; invalid values are logged but not thrown, and missing/empty limits are silently omitted.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the `limit` column from RSVP form JSON (table export) is parsed as a positive integer and applied as the `maxlength` HTML attribute only on elements created by `createInput` and `createTextArea` helpers. Invalid limit values are logged via `window.lana` without throwing errors; this graceful degradation ensures backward compatibility. Selects, checkboxes, and other input types do not receive the `limit` field. Configs without a `limit` column or with empty/invalid values behave identically to pre-feature versions (no `maxlength` attribute).

nodes.summary: Sessions-hub auto-registration integrates RSVP form submission through events-form block; chrono-box conditionally suppresses first schedule item when no conditions match.
nodes.details: The sessions-hub block now triggers auto-registration by delegating form submission to the events-form block rather than handling RSVP directly. This pattern centralizes form field validation and payload preparation in events-form. Additionally, chrono-box (timing-framework) implements conditional rendering: the first schedule item is skipped if no time-condition rules match, preventing empty or placeholder schedule displays. Both patterns live in event-libs/v1/blocks/ and should be followed when extending RSVP or schedule rendering flows.

nodes.summary: Placeholder syntax for array iteration ([[@array(path.attr)separator]]) and conditional rendering ([[condition?(true):(false)]]) with BlockMediator store integration (@BM.storeName.property) enables dynamic content decoration in event templates.
nodes.details: The events-milo frontend supports two core decoration patterns: (1) Array iteration via [[@array(metadata-path.attribute)separator]] syntax in events/scripts/utils.js, which extracts attributes from object arrays and joins with custom separators (default: space); (2) Conditional rendering via [[condition?(true-content):(false-content)]] supporting equality/inequality checks, AND (&) and OR (||) operators, and reactive BlockMediator store references (@BM.storeName.property). Store references automatically subscribe to changes and re-render content. These patterns are processed by parseMetadataPath, parseConditionalContent, and content-update.js. Use these for dynamic event state display (registration status, capacity, user type) without modifying template HTML.

nodes.summary: Do not pass user-supplied HTML strings through Milo's createTag() when building modal content; use plain-text helpers to avoid unintended focusable elements.
nodes.details: In profile-cards, speaker `title` field was passed directly to `createTag()`, which interprets strings as HTML. This caused markup like `<a>` tags to render before the modal's intended first focusable (`h2.card-name`), breaking Milo's `FOCUSABLES` selector and causing incorrect focus-visible styling on modal open. Solution: extract `modalJobTitlePlainText()` helper and use it exclusively in `buildModalContent()` for `.card-title` elements. Grid card rendering (which does not use modals) remains unchanged. Mirror Milo's `FOCUSABLES` selector in unit tests to verify focus order.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: Session Page is the durable standalone page per session at /sessions/[slug]-[code].html, the permanent on-demand destination
nodes.details: Session Page is auto-generated from Rainfocus. URL pattern: /max/2026/sessions/[title-slug]-[sessioncode].html. Three states: Pre-session (full detail layout, Add to schedule / Favorite / Share), Live (Watch Now CTA routes to Channel), On-demand (video player above content, autoplays; Add to schedule hidden). Post-event: all Session Guide cards route here; modals retired. Data source: Rainfocus (slug, code, metadata, video ID, flags, start time, duration).

nodes.summary: Session Guide is the consolidated session discovery layer on the Homepage, replacing Sessions Hub, Agenda, and My Schedule
nodes.details: Session Guide is embedded on the event Homepage (drawer on mobile, panel on desktop). Four views: All Sessions (organized by Channel), My Sessions (schedule + .ics download + AI agent entry), My Favorites (T1 only), On Demand (T1 only). Routes to Channel Homepage experience when a session is live; routes to Session Page when on-demand. Post-event: accessible as full page at /sessions.html — session cards route to Session Pages; modals retired.

nodes.summary: Profile card images without altText must be marked decorative with alt="" and role="presentation" for screen reader accessibility.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/profile-cards/profile-cards.js, member images are conditionally rendered: if altText exists, use it as the alt attribute; if altText is absent, set alt="" and role="presentation" to signal to assistive technology that the image is decorative and should be skipped. Social icons retain their platform-specific alt text (e.g., alt="${platform} logo") and are unaffected. This pattern ensures WCAG 2.1 Level A compliance for images that carry no semantic meaning.

nodes.summary: Page metadata (PPN) fields require explicit user acknowledgment before save; use sentinel id 'no-${fieldKey}' to distinguish explicit *No* selection from unset state.
nodes.details: EventFormData tracks metadataFieldAcknowledged (UI-only boolean map) to enforce that users must open each product/category dropdown and choose either a value or the *No* option before draft/publish. The *No* option uses stable id no-${fieldKey} (not startsWith('No ')) to persist correctly. After API load or successful save, hydrate acknowledgments so existing events remain usable without forced re-picking. Validate page-metadata fields only when catalogue fields exist. This prevents silent defaults and ensures intentional metadata decisions.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. nodes.summary: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField validation rules were relaxed to accept legacy user-typed formats in the database; request and response validation kept symmetric pending future RSVP form redesign and data normalization.
nodes.details: In openapi.json, PhoneNumber pattern changed from `^\+?[0-9]+$` to `^\+?[0-9 ().-]+$` (maxLength 20→30) to accept spaces, parens, and dashes; AttendeeTextField maxLength raised from 100 to 200 across 10 fields (companyName, organizationName, dietaryRestrictions, invitedBy, etc.). This was a production blocker: 13% of ~1,650 attendee records violated the stricter MWPW-188918 rules, causing GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees to fail express-openapi-validator with HTTP 418. Request and response validation were kept symmetric intentionally—future phone canonicalization or RSVP form validation tightening can re-constrain the spec independently. Data normalization (216 malformed phones) is out of scope and tracked separately.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: Speaker photo hydration requires explicit imagesMgr.list() join; photos are stored as separate DynamoDB records (sk: imagekind#speaker-photo) and must be fetched and attached to speaker objects.
nodes.details: In src/routes/events/speakers/read.js, both GET /v1/events/:eventId/speakers (list) and GET /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId (single) endpoints must call imagesMgr.list() in parallel and join photo records onto speaker objects by matching speaker ID. This pattern is already correctly implemented in GET /v1/series/:seriesId/speakers and should be mirrored across all speaker-returning endpoints. Speakers without uploaded photos should return without a photo field (not null or error). Omitting this hydration step leaves the photo field missing from the response contract.

nodes.summary: Orphaned page cleanup is triggered synchronously at Kinesis record-processing time by detecting detailPagePath changes via event history, not deferred to the handler loop.
nodes.details: When a published, liveUpdate event is modified, EventDataStreamProcessor calls EventService.getEventHistory(eventId) to fetch the event's prior states. findLastPublishedHistory walks the history array newest-to-oldest, skipping entries whose timestamp matches the current modificationTime (race-condition guard), and returns the first entry with published=true && liveUpdate=true. If that entry's detailPagePath differs from the current one, sendEventDataToWebhook is called immediately with isDeleteEvent=true and the old path, allowing downstream consumers (e.g. SharePoint) to clean up orphaned pages without waiting for the main handler. History fetch failures are caught and logged; processing continues normally (no Kinesis retry). Timestamp comparison uses String() coercion on both sides to handle type differences between DynamoDB-unmarshalled numbers and history API values.

nodes.summary: Production event publishing requires explicit user confirmation via AlertDialog before calling publishEvent; dev/stage builds skip this gate.
nodes.details: In EventForm.tsx, when ENVIRONMENT=prod, both handleComplete and executeSaveWithUrl paths funnel through requestPublishAfterUrlResolved, which opens a Spectrum 2 AlertDialog for user acceptance before invoking publishEvent. The extraPayload ref is cleared only on confirm or Cancel, not in onOpenChange, to preserve the payload if close handlers fire before onPrimaryAction executes. This pattern prevents accidental production event publication.

nodes.summary: Scope configs (rsvp, locales, customAttributes) are the authoritative source for event metadata; publishing profiles are deprecated but retained for backward compatibility during migration.
nodes.details: Events created under Creative Events (25f26faa-f8e2-4e99-b341-81a3995ef9af) and Enterprise Events (d758a3bc-ff31-4bfe-a2f5-343f074aec6c) scopes must define four config types: rsvp (pool of form fields), locales (localeNames, localeUrlCodes), and customAttributes (with primaryProductName and promotionalItems attributes). The Kinesis processor (events-kinesis-processor/ServiceProcessor.applyRelatedData) must call GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs to hydrate event.locales, event.customAttributesConfig, and event.rsvpConfig at stream-processing time; event DDB records store only user selections (rsvpFormFields, customAttributes[] with valueId), not full definitions. Publishing profiles remain in the payload for backward compat but are no longer the source of truth. hoolihan-webhooks must read primary product from event.customAttributes[] where attribute='primaryProductName', promotional items from customAttributes[] where attribute='promotionalItems', RSVP pool from event.rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields[], and locales from event.locales.localeNames/localeUrlCodes.

nodes.summary: Do not replace entire itemData objects in DynamoDB PUT operations without preserving required fields; use merge/patch semantics or enforce all required fields in the request schema.
nodes.details: Publishing profiles were created with status: 'active', but PUT /v1/publishing-profiles/{profileId} requests that omitted status would replace the entire stored itemData, removing the field. nodes.summary: Response validation must be permissive for legacy attendee data; request-side validation is decoupled and handled separately by RSVP forms.
nodes.details: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField schemas in GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees responses were over-constrained (pattern: ^\+?[0-9]+$, maxLength: 20 for phone; pattern rejecting all HTML for text fields with maxLength: 100), causing 12.8% of production attendee records to fail HTTP 418 validation. nodes.summary: Campaign-aware RSVP registration: when campaignId URL param is present, fetch campaign capacity and apply waitlist rules before attendee creation.
nodes.details: In esp-controller.js, the getAndCreateAndAddAttendee flow checks for campaignId in the attendee payload. If present and event is not full, call getCampaign(eventId, campaignId) to fetch campaign capacity (attendeeLimit, attendeeCount, waitlistAttendeeCount). Apply waitlist logic: if attendeeLimit === attendeeCount, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount > 0, mark waitlisted; if attendeeLimit > attendeeCount and waitlistAttendeeCount === 0, register normally. If no attendeeLimit, pass campaignId without campaign logic. Skip campaign lookup when event is already full. campaignId is sanitized in events-form.js (regex ^[\w-]{1,128}$) and added to EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in data-utils.js so it flows into the event attendee API body.

nodes.summary: ESP event-speaker PUT body contract is { speakerId, speakerType, ordinal, creationTime, modificationTime } and nothing else
nodes.details: Per ESP OpenAPI, /v1/events/:eventId/speakers/:speakerId PUT accepts only those five fields. When using callWithDependency's body-builder, fall back to dependentData per-field: body.X ?? dependentData.X. creationTime and modificationTime are server-issued; do not let callers override them. The same pattern applies to all ESP PUTs on speaker resources.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.

The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: Image updates in Kinesis stream lack eventId in payload; extract from DynamoDB partition key instead of relying on newData field.

Without this extraction, image updates fail to propagate to the event record until the event itself is modified. This pattern applies to all image-related Kinesis processing in the events-kinesis-processor Lambda.

This establishes that status queries are scoped to registration state alone, not full attendee metadata or event context. The endpoint supports both explicit attendeeId and 'me' (current user) path parameters. Future status-related queries should follow this minimal-payload pattern rather than returning full attendee objects.

nodes.summary: Attendees resource has dual CRUD surfaces: standalone /v1/attendees/* for lifecycle management, and nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* for event-specific membership operations only.
nodes.details: The attendees CRUD operations split across two route hierarchies: /v1/attendees/{create,read,update,delete}.js handle attendee entity lifecycle (create new attendee, read attendee details, update attendee profile, delete attendee). The nested /v1/events/:eventId/attendees/* routes (in src/routes/events/attendees/) handle only event membership: POST adds an *existing* attendee to an event (does not create attendees), GET lists attendees for an event, DELETE removes attendee from event, PUT updates attendee's event-specific state. This separation prevents attendee creation from being coupled to event enrollment. Enforce via attendeesMgr.js and eventsMgr.js: standalone routes call attendeesMgr directly; nested routes validate attendee exists before calling eventsMgr membership methods.

nodes.summary: ESP OpenAPI spec must define response schemas for all HTTP status codes returned by endpoints, including 200; missing schemas cause runtime validation failures.
nodes.details: The events-service-platform validates responses against the OpenAPI spec at runtime. If an endpoint returns a 200 status code but the spec lacks a schema definition for that code, the request fails with 'no schema defined for status code' error. This applies to POST /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees and all other endpoints. Always add response schema definitions (including status code, content-type, and body shape) to src/api/openapi.json when adding or modifying endpoints, even for success cases.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: Consent suite visibility and country-region capture follow a locale-aware, metadata-driven pattern: force-consent-collection metadata controls suite visibility; country picker data-country-code maps to payload.countryRegion; consent index URL uses locale-prefixed fallback pattern matching promotional-content.

This establishes the contract: force-consent-collection is a boolean metadata flag that overrides guest-only consent visibility, and country selection always populates countryRegion when the suite is shown.

nodes.summary: Event attendee route handlers use explicit field mappings instead of spreading req.body, causing OpenAPI-validated fields to silently drop before persistence.
nodes.details: The attendee CRUD routes (create.js, update.js, read.js) in src/routes/events/attendees/ build eventAttendee objects by hand-picking fields rather than spreading req.body. This means fields validated by the OpenAPI spec (e.g., requiresTicket) can pass validation but never reach DynamoDB or the response. nodes.details: EMC (web-src/src/) is a React 18 + TypeScript + React Spectrum S2 SPA deployed via Adobe App Builder. There is no backend in this repo. All API calls route through services/api.ts (ApiService) and cachedApi wrapper: GET requests use 10s caching with request dedup and pattern-based invalidation; all mutations require input validation via validateString()/validateObject() before dispatch; all fetch calls pass through safeFetch() with ALLOWED_HOSTS validation. Two external backends: Adobe ESP (events/series/speakers endpoints) and ESL (lifecycle/venues/attendees). Auth uses Bearer token (IMS in prod, dev token locally) + x-gw-ims-org-id header. Dry-run mode available via apiService.enableDryRun(). Form state (EventForm, SeriesForm) persists to sessionStorage with debounced auto-save; multi-step FormWizard uses useEventFormComponent hook lifecycle (onGatherPayload, onAfterSave, onLoadResponse, validate) for step registration.

nodes.summary: RSVP form field configuration requires option-level granularity (subset selection, ordering) that is non-trivial on the BE and easy to underestimate

Any pod touching RSVP or dynamic form-field configuration should scope BE option-level support as an explicit, separate work item.

nodes.summary: RSVP field option panels render inline within the field card with conditional icon toggle; drag interactions collapse all open panels to enforce mutual exclusivity.
nodes.details: In RegistrationFieldsComponent.tsx, option panels for RSVP fields (select, multi-select) now render as children inside the field card border rather than as sibling elements below. The icon highlights in selection-ring color when open. Starting a field drag operation collapses all open option panels—this is a deliberate UX constraint to prevent simultaneous drag and panel interactions. Option rows no longer have individual borders; drag-over ring feedback is retained. Fields without options have no list icon and no extra column gap.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.

In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the createForm() function must call trim() on field names from the form config before using them in visible.includes(f.field) and required.includes(lowkey.field) checks. nodes.summary: Attendee API field `requiresTicket` is the canonical name; prior `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed across routes, manager, and OpenAPI spec as part of generalization.
nodes.details: The field `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed to `requiresTicket` on `EventAttendeeBody` and `EventAttendee` schemas (MWPW-194794, PRs #954–#958). This change propagated through: (1) OpenAPI spec in `src/api/openapi.json`, (2) attendee manager in `src/managers/attendeesMgr.js`, and (3) all attendee routes (`src/routes/events/attendees/{create,read,update}.js`). nodes.summary: React Spectrum 2 Tabs component can crash when overflow/collapse unmounts its internal TabListStateContext; use SegmentedControl + conditional rendering instead.
nodes.details: S2 horizontal Tabs on the Registrations page (/registrations) can enter an overflow/collapse path that unmounts the react-aria-components Tabs shell, leaving TabListStateContext null and causing 'Cannot read properties of null (reading selectedKey)' crashes. Replace with SegmentedControl + SegmentedControlItem (the established EMC pattern) paired with selectedTab state to conditionally render the three sections (Registrations, Campaigns, Sessions). This avoids the context unmounting issue entirely. See web-src/src/pages/Registrations/Registrations.tsx for the applied pattern.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: Placeholder syntax for array iteration ([[@array(path.attr)separator]]) and conditional rendering ([[condition?(true):(false)]]) with BlockMediator store integration (@BM.storeName.property) enables dynamic content decoration in event templates.
nodes.details: The events-milo frontend supports two core decoration patterns: (1) Array iteration via [[@array(metadata-path.attribute)separator]] syntax in events/scripts/utils.js, which extracts attributes from object arrays and joins with custom separators (default: space); (2) Conditional rendering via [[condition?(true-content):(false-content)]] supporting equality/inequality checks, AND (&) and OR (||) operators, and reactive BlockMediator store references (@BM.storeName.property). Store references automatically subscribe to changes and re-render content. These patterns are processed by parseMetadataPath, parseConditionalContent, and content-update.js. Use these for dynamic event state display (registration status, capacity, user type) without modifying template HTML.

nodes.summary: Event speaker PUT request body must be contract-shaped; do not spread raw GET response into PUT payload.
nodes.details: The API service layer enforces a specific payload shape for speaker PUT operations (web-src/src/services/api.ts). When updating event speakers, construct the request body to match the server's expected contract rather than spreading the GET response directly. This prevents field mismatches and validation failures. See Sessions and EventForm components for correct usage patterns.

nodes.summary: Implicit consent on RSVP is recorded by populating the existing contactMethods array when consent UI shows messaging only (no checkboxes), sourced from authored implicit-consent metadata.
nodes.details: When an RSVP form has consent messaging but no explicit checkboxes, call parseImplicitConsentChannels() to extract channel names from the implicit-consent metadata (checked in order: fragment <meta>, query param implicitConsent/implicit_consent, or page meta), then apply applyImplicitContactMethodsToPayload() to inject those channels into the attendee payload's contactMethods array before submitForm validation. This reuses the existing getBaseAttendeePayload / ESL pipeline without adding new attendee attributes. The metadata resolution and payload mutation happen in events-form.js after loadFragment but before API submission.

nodes.summary: RichTextEditor export must use getSemanticHTML() to produce portable <ul>/<ol> instead of Quill's internal data-list markup; normalize NBSP variants on load/export for API consistency.
nodes.details: In web-src/src/components/shared/RichTextEditor.tsx, call getSemanticHTML() instead of root.innerHTML when exporting editor content so that bullet lists serialize as semantic <ul> and numbered lists as <ol>, not Quill 2's internal <ol data-list="…"> format. Restrict formats whitelist to toolbar capabilities (bold, italic, underline, strike, list, indent, align, link) to prevent pasted content from retaining unwanted styling (color, background, font, size).

nodes.summary: HTML/script injection in attendee string fields must be blocked at the API schema layer using reusable NoTagsString validators, not in application code.
nodes.details: Define injection-safe OpenAPI schemas (`NoTagsString`, `AttendeeName`, `AttendeeTextField`, `SpecialRequirements`, `PhoneNumber`) in `src/api/openapi.json` and apply them to all attendee string fields via `express-openapi-validator`. This centralizes validation at the API boundary and prevents downstream code from receiving malicious payloads. `BaseAttendee` fields (`firstName`, `lastName`, `companyName`, `countryRegion`, `zipPostalCode`, `organizationName`, `title`, `primarySocialMediaAccount`, `dietaryRestrictions`, `executiveAssistantName`, `mobilePhone`, `businessPhone`, `specialRequirements`) and `EventAttendee` fields (`firstName`, `lastName`, `invitedBy`, `campaignId`) must all use these schemas. Do not rely on application-layer sanitization or assume client-side filtering is sufficient.

nodes.summary: Do not pass user-supplied HTML strings through Milo's createTag() when building modal content; use plain-text helpers to avoid unintended focusable elements.
nodes.details: In profile-cards, speaker `title` field was passed directly to `createTag()`, which interprets strings as HTML. This caused markup like `<a>` tags to render before the modal's intended first focusable (`h2.card-name`), breaking Milo's `FOCUSABLES` selector and causing incorrect focus-visible styling on modal open. Solution: extract `modalJobTitlePlainText()` helper and use it exclusively in `buildModalContent()` for `.card-title` elements. Grid card rendering (which does not use modals) remains unchanged. Mirror Milo's `FOCUSABLES` selector in unit tests to verify focus order.

nodes.summary: Do not assume social icon sources have uniform shape; ESP metadata supplies objects while static authoring supplies DOM anchors—decorateSocialIcons must handle both.
nodes.details: After the static-authoring refactor, decorateSocialIcons was narrowed to accept only HTMLAnchorElement, causing ESP metadata-driven speakers' socialLinks (supplied as { link, serviceName } objects) to be silently skipped. The fix restores support for anchors, link objects, and string URLs: clone anchors with inherited attributes, createTag for metadata objects with aria-label derived from serviceName or platform detection. Also restore the socialLinks || socialMedia fallback chain when decorating. This pattern applies to any block accepting speaker/profile data from both static HTML and ESP metadata sources.

nodes.summary: Attendee string fields are validated via reusable OpenAPI schemas (NoTagsString, AttendeeName, AttendeeTextField, SpecialRequirements, PhoneNumber) enforced by express-openapi-validator at the API layer to prevent injection attacks and enforce length limits.
nodes.details: All attendee string inputs must pass schema validation in src/api/openapi.json before reaching business logic. NoTagsString rejects values containing `<…>` (HTML/script tags). AttendeeName (firstName, lastName) max 30 chars; AttendeeTextField (companyName, countryRegion, organizationName, title, dietaryRestrictions, etc.) max 100 chars; SpecialRequirements max 1000 chars; PhoneNumber (mobilePhone, businessPhone) digits + `+` only, max 20 chars. Website (format: uri) and executiveAssistantEmail (format: email) use existing OpenAPI format constraints; contactMethod uses enum. Validation is declarative in openapi.json and enforced by express-openapi-validator middleware — do not add runtime validation in handlers.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Tokens are duplicated under html[data-color-scheme='dark'] selector to ensure first paint and post-effect hydration alignment. Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: Do not use non-unique identifiers (consentId) as HTML select option values when the same ID appears across multiple rows; use a unique key (countryCode) as value and store the non-unique ID in a data attribute.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, the consent country selector was setting `select.value = consentId`, which caused HTML's native select behavior to match only the first option with that value, leading to wrong country pre-population when the consent-query-index contained duplicate consentIds across countries. The fix: set `select.value = countryCode` (unique per country), store `consentId` in `data-consent-id` attribute on each option, then retrieve it via `selectedOption.dataset.consentId` during form submission. This pattern applies to any multi-row lookup where a non-unique identifier must be preserved for payload submission but a unique key is needed for DOM selection.

nodes.summary: Response validation must be permissive for legacy attendee data; request-side validation is decoupled and handled separately by RSVP forms.
nodes.details: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField schemas in GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees responses were over-constrained (pattern: ^\+?[0-9]+$, maxLength: 20 for phone; pattern rejecting all HTML for text fields with maxLength: 100), causing 12.8% of production attendee records to fail HTTP 418 validation. The fix relaxes response schemas (PhoneNumber: drop pattern, maxLength 30; AttendeeTextField: newline-tolerant pattern ^(?![\s\S]*<[^>]*>)[\s\S]*$, maxLength 200) while explicitly documenting that form-side input validation remains the responsibility of RSVP-form frontends. This resolves the architectural tension: the service layer must accept and return legacy data as-is; sanitization and strict validation belong upstream.

nodes.summary: Hydrator pattern: read event metadata from HTML meta tags and transform into block-ready HTML structure during page initialization.
nodes.details: The hydrator logic in event-libs/v1/hydrate/hydrate.js and event-libs/v1/hydrate/image-links.js reads structured data from <meta> tags (e.g., event title, date, speaker info) and generates the DOM structure required by the image-links block before the block's decorate() function runs. This decouples content authoring (meta tags in page head) from block rendering (image-links.js), allowing authors to define event data once and have it hydrated into multiple block types. The pattern applies to any block that needs pre-computed or externally-sourced data at page load time.

nodes.summary: Do not rely on :focus:not(:focus-visible) CSS to suppress focus rings when Milo's getModal uses .focus({ focusVisible: true }) — the flag forces :focus-visible to match regardless of input method.
nodes.details: Milo's getModal helper focuses the first FOCUSABLE element using .focus({ focusVisible: true }), which explicitly forces :focus-visible to match even on programmatic focus. CSS rules like :focus:not(:focus-visible) cannot suppress this ring. Instead, ensure the first FOCUSABLE in modal DOM order is an element where outline: none is already applied (e.g., a heading with tabindex="0"), or add outline: none to the element that will receive initial focus. In profile-cards/profile-cards.js, the fix was to add tabindex="0" to the card-name h2 in buildModalContent so it precedes social links in focus order, and the existing .card-name:focus { outline: none; } rule suppresses the ring.

nodes.summary: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField validation rules were relaxed to accept legacy user-typed formats in the database; request and response validation kept symmetric pending future RSVP form redesign and data normalization.
nodes.details: In openapi.json, PhoneNumber pattern changed from `^\+?[0-9]+$` to `^\+?[0-9 ().-]+$` (maxLength 20→30) to accept spaces, parens, and dashes; AttendeeTextField maxLength raised from 100 to 200 across 10 fields (companyName, organizationName, dietaryRestrictions, invitedBy, etc.). This was a production blocker: 13% of ~1,650 attendee records violated the stricter MWPW-188918 rules, causing GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees to fail express-openapi-validator with HTTP 418. Request and response validation were kept symmetric intentionally—future phone canonicalization or RSVP form validation tightening can re-constrain the spec independently. Data normalization (216 malformed phones) is out of scope and tracked separately.

nodes.summary: Array iteration placeholder syntax `[[@array(path.attribute)separator]]` with flexible concatenation, object attribute extraction, and nested path resolution in event-libs metadata system.
nodes.details: The `[[@array(metadata-path.attribute)separator]]` syntax enables iteration over array metadata with configurable separators (comma, pipe, bullet, newline, or space-default). When an attribute is specified (e.g., `speakers.name`), the system extracts that field from each object; without an attribute, objects convert to JSON strings. Implementation lives in `event-libs/v1/utils/utils.js` within `parseMetadataPath` function, integrated with `updateTextNode` and `updateTextContent`. Supports nested paths like `event-data.speakers.name`. Error cases (empty arrays, missing metadata, invalid paths) return empty strings. This replaces manual comma-concatenated metadata strings with structured array/object metadata.

nodes.summary: AttendeeTextField maxLength relaxed from 100 to 200 chars to prevent ESL from being a stricter validation gate than upstream ESP for invitedBy and campaignId fields.
nodes.details: ESP encountered PROD failures when legacy attendee records exceeded the 100-char cap on AttendeeTextField in GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees responses. ESL's POST /events/{eventId}/attendees/{attendeeId} validates invitedBy and campaignId via the same AttendeeTextField schema ($ref in openapi.json:2006). To maintain schema alignment and prevent ESL from rejecting valid payloads that ESP accepts, maxLength was bumped to 200. The injection pattern (^(?!.*<[^>]*>).*$) remains unchanged. PhoneNumber and mobilePhone/businessPhone fields were not ported because they have zero $refs in ESL's spec.

nodes.summary: Event attendee route handlers use explicit field mappings instead of spreading req.body, causing OpenAPI-validated fields to silently drop before persistence.
nodes.details: The attendee CRUD routes (create.js, update.js, read.js) in src/routes/events/attendees/ build eventAttendee objects by hand-picking fields rather than spreading req.body. This means fields validated by the OpenAPI spec (e.g., requiresTicket) can pass validation but never reach DynamoDB or the response. When adding a new attendee field, it must be explicitly added to all three route handlers' field mappings, or it will be silently dropped. Use explicit field mappings only when you need to exclude or transform fields; otherwise, spread req.body and filter at the schema layer.

nodes.summary: Do not use allOf compositions for simple type constraints in OpenAPI schemas; flatten to direct type + constraint fields to avoid express-openapi-validator v5 response validation bugs.
nodes.details: express-openapi-validator v5 with validateResponses: true incorrectly treats optional response fields defined via $ref → allOf (where a sub-schema specifies type: string) as required, causing validation to fail on absent optional fields. Instead of composing schemas like AttendeeName via allOf with a $ref to NoTagsString plus maxLength, define the schema directly with type: string, pattern, and maxLength in a single object. This avoids the validator's incorrect required-property inference while maintaining semantic equivalence. Applied to AttendeeName, AttendeeTextField, and SpecialRequirements in src/api/openapi.json.

nodes.summary: Do not apply strict input validation schemas to GET response bodies; use separate input and output schemas to preserve backward compatibility with legacy data.
nodes.details: In events-service-platform, attendee phone fields (`mobilePhone`, `businessPhone`) must support two schemas: a strict `PhoneNumberInput` pattern `^[+\d\s\-().]+$` for POST/PUT writes, and a permissive `PhoneNumber` schema for GET responses. Implement this via OpenAPI `allOf` composition on request bodies (`requestBodies/BaseAttendee`, `requestBodies/Attendee`) while keeping response schemas unchanged. This prevents validation errors on legacy data (e.g. `"None"`, `"N/A"`) that exists in the database but should not be accepted on new writes. See `src/api/openapi.json` for the schema structure and `src/api/test/openapi-attendees-validation.test.js` for validation test patterns.

nodes.summary: Do not call closeModal() without passing the modal DOM element argument; it causes TypeError when modal.js tries to read the element's id property.
nodes.details: In sessions-hub.js, closeModal() requires a modal DOM element parameter. Previously, closeModal() was invoked without arguments, causing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')' in Milo's modal.js. The fix: capture the dialog element returned by getModal() and pass it to all closeModal() calls. This pattern applies to any Milo modal integration — always bind the element reference before invoking close operations.
