Critically, this field is NOT included in Splash custom field mappings — it remains local to the events platform. Field visibility/requirement is controlled by Event Marketers at the console level (not API-enforced), meaning the API accepts the field regardless of event cloud-type. This establishes the boundary: events-service-platform owns storage and retrieval; console owns form presentation logic; Splash integration is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.
nodes.details: When submitting event-attendee payloads for RSVP, include `requiresSxswTicket` boolean when SXSW ticket filter applies (#140). Implicit consent for new registrations is recorded via the `contactMethods` field in the payload (MWPW-194036, #126). In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.summary: RSVP button state machine: six mutually-exclusive states (loading, default, registered, waitlisted, to-waitlist, event-closed) driven by authentication, capacity, and registration status; text and accessibility managed via dictionary keys and tabindex.
nodes.details: RSVP buttons in event-libs use hash patterns (#rsvp-form, #webinar-marketo-form) to trigger decorateEvent processing. State transitions are: Loading (disabled, tabindex=-1) → Default (enabled) → one of {Registered, Waitlisted, To Waitlist, Event Closed} based on user auth (allow-guest-registration meta), event capacity (ESP API), and waitlist config (allow-wait-listing meta). Each state maps to a dictionary key (rsvp-loading-cta-text, registered-cta-text, waitlist-cta-text, event-full-cta-text, etc.). Form 400 errors distinguish event-full vs campaign-full (via ?campaign URL param) and whether waitlisting is enabled, using separate error keys (event-full-error-msg, campaign-full-no-waitlist-error-msg, etc.). Custom button text uses pipe separator (text|fallback). State updates are reactive via BlockMediator subscriptions.

nodes.summary: Event-attendee payload fields must be explicitly listed in EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER to be sent to ESL's addAttendeeToEvent endpoint.
nodes.details: The EVENT_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER in event-libs/v1/utils/data-utils.js acts as an allowlist for which form fields are included in the event-attendee payload sent to ESL. New checkbox or form fields (e.g., requiresSxswTicket, shareInfoWithPartners) must be added to this filter in getEventAttendeePayload() to be transmitted. Additionally, when gating form fields via rsvp-form-fields metadata in events-form.js, new sheet fields must be listed in the visible array to render; unlisted fields are silently dropped.

nodes.summary: RSVP and custom attribute option values use { value, label } pairs: value is the locale-independent DB key, label is the localizable display text.
nodes.details: RSVP form field options and custom attribute values now follow a two-part structure: `value` (immutable, locale-independent identifier used for DB storage and API contracts) and `label` (localizable, user-facing display text). RsvpLocalizationsEditor matches translated options by value key rather than positional index, ensuring localization stability across option reordering. FieldOptionsEditor and CustomAttributesEditor both support bulk edit and semicolon-paste workflows. This pattern applies across console/src/components/configs/ (ScopeConfigsView.jsx, FieldOptionsEditor, RsvpLocalizationsEditor, CustomAttributesEditor) and test fixtures (addRsvpConfig.js, addCustomAttributesConfig.js).

nodes.summary: Scope configs unify RSVP forms, locales, and custom attributes under a single typed config system with scope-inherited hierarchy (org → team) and full-replace merge semantics.
nodes.details: All configuration for the events console — RSVP form fields, locale definitions, and custom attribute definitions — is managed through a single `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs` API with `type` field (e.g., 'rsvp', 'locales', 'custom-attributes'). Configs inherit down the scope hierarchy with full-replace merge per type. Frontend reads merged configs via `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs` or `GET /v1/series/{seriesId}/configs` with optional `?type=` filter. Custom attributes are a config type, not a separate entity. Admin management uses POST/PUT/DELETE on `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs/{configId}` and requires `config:read`, `config:write`, or `config:delete` permissions.

nodes.summary: Invite-only events gate RSVP behind `inviteOnly` flag and campaign URL param; replace button with text message rather than disable.
nodes.details: The invite-only RSVP feature gates registration on two conditions: (1) an `inviteOnly` event flag from the backend, and (2) a campaign URL parameter. When both conditions are met, the RSVP button is replaced with a text message instead of being disabled. This pattern prevents accidental user confusion and clarifies that the event is not available for self-service registration. Check `event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js` for the gating logic and button replacement implementation.

nodes.summary: Attendee API field `requiresTicket` is the canonical name; prior `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed across routes, manager, and OpenAPI spec as part of generalization.
nodes.details: The field `requiresSxswTicket` was renamed to `requiresTicket` on `EventAttendeeBody` and `EventAttendee` schemas (MWPW-194794, PRs #954–#958). This change propagated through: (1) OpenAPI spec in `src/api/openapi.json`, (2) attendee manager in `src/managers/attendeesMgr.js`, and (3) all attendee routes (`src/routes/events/attendees/{create,read,update}.js`). The rename signals a shift from event-specific (SXSW) to generic event semantics. Future attendee schema changes should use `requiresTicket` as the canonical field name.

nodes.summary: Scope configs (rsvp, locales, customAttributes) are the authoritative source for event metadata; publishing profiles are deprecated but retained for backward compatibility during migration.
nodes.details: Events created under Creative Events (25f26faa-f8e2-4e99-b341-81a3995ef9af) and Enterprise Events (d758a3bc-ff31-4bfe-a2f5-343f074aec6c) scopes must define four config types: rsvp (pool of form fields), locales (localeNames, localeUrlCodes), and customAttributes (with primaryProductName and promotionalItems attributes). The Kinesis processor (events-kinesis-processor/ServiceProcessor.applyRelatedData) must call GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs to hydrate event.locales, event.customAttributesConfig, and event.rsvpConfig at stream-processing time; event DDB records store only user selections (rsvpFormFields, customAttributes[] with valueId), not full definitions. Publishing profiles remain in the payload for backward compat but are no longer the source of truth. hoolihan-webhooks must read primary product from event.customAttributes[] where attribute='primaryProductName', promotional items from customAttributes[] where attribute='promotionalItems', RSVP pool from event.rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields[], and locales from event.locales.localeNames/localeUrlCodes.

nodes.summary: ESL attendee schemas must stay synchronized with ESP spec; use generic field names (requiresTicket) at ESL layer even when ESP uses domain-specific names (requiresSxswTicket).
nodes.details: When ESP (events-service-platform) adds a new attendee field, ESL (events-service-layer) must mirror it in both EventAttendeeBody (request schema in src/api/openapi.json) and EventAttendee (response schema). ESL renames domain-specific ESP fields to generic names for reusability—e.g., ESP's requiresSxswTicket becomes requiresTicket at ESL. Since ESL passes attendee bodies directly through to ESP without transformation, the schema addition alone is sufficient; no transformer logic is required. Bump the OpenAPI spec version when adding fields.

nodes.summary: RSVP field option panels render inline within the field card with conditional icon toggle; drag interactions collapse all open panels to enforce mutual exclusivity.
nodes.details: In RegistrationFieldsComponent.tsx, option panels for RSVP fields (select, multi-select) now render as children inside the field card border rather than as sibling elements below. The expand/collapse trigger is a ListBulleted icon in a 5th grid column (only rendered for fields with selectable options via rsvpFieldDefinitions.ts). The icon highlights in selection-ring color when open. Starting a field drag operation collapses all open option panels—this is a deliberate UX constraint to prevent simultaneous drag and panel interactions. Option rows no longer have individual borders; drag-over ring feedback is retained. Fields without options have no list icon and no extra column gap.

nodes.summary: Localization overlays on RSVP forms: base field definitions + per-locale label/placeholder overrides
nodes.details: Implemented by fe-agent-registration: The RSVP form schema has a base layer (field types, ordering, validation rules) and per-locale overlays that override only label and placeholder strings. The FormRenderer selects the overlay matching the user's locale, falling back to the base layer. This keeps form structure consistent across locales while allowing full translation of user-facing text.

nodes.summary: Registration form preview mode renders the form with sample data without creating records — essential for organizer testing
nodes.details: Implemented by fe-agent-registration: The RSVP form editor includes a 'Preview' button that renders the FormRenderer in read-only mode with sample data. The preview uses the same rendering path as the live form but submits to a no-op endpoint. This lets organizers see exactly how their form will look before publishing, including locale overlays and custom attributes.

nodes.summary: RSVP API / EMC discrepancy (decision)
nodes.details: Decision by cli-user: EMC has per-option RSVP UI state; event API only has rsvpFormFields visible/required.

nodes.summary: Page metadata (PPN) fields require explicit user acknowledgment before save; use sentinel id 'no-${fieldKey}' to distinguish explicit *No* selection from unset state.
nodes.details: EventFormData tracks metadataFieldAcknowledged (UI-only boolean map) to enforce that users must open each product/category dropdown and choose either a value or the *No* option before draft/publish. The *No* option uses stable id no-${fieldKey} (not startsWith('No ')) to persist correctly. After API load or successful save, hydrate acknowledgments so existing events remain usable without forced re-picking. Validate page-metadata fields only when catalogue fields exist. This prevents silent defaults and ensures intentional metadata decisions.

nodes.summary: RSVP button and form 400-error handling must respect campaign capacity when ?campaign URL param is present and valid, falling back to event capacity otherwise, with campaign-specific error messages and UI state.
nodes.details: When a valid campaign ID is present in the URL (?campaign=...), use getCampaign() to fetch campaign capacity and apply it to both RSVP button state (updateRSVPButtonState in decorate.js) and form 400-error handling (buildErrorMsg and submit handler in events-form.js). If campaign fetch fails or campaign ID is invalid (validate via CAMPAIGN_ID_PATTERN in constances.js), fall back to event capacity. On 400 response with campaign present, use campaign-full-error-msg or campaign-full-no-waitlist-error-msg keys and update submit button to waitlist or event-full state (disabled if no waitlist) to keep copy and UI consistent. This ensures campaign-level capacity gates take precedence over event-level gates when applicable.

nodes.summary: Sessions-hub auto-registration integrates RSVP form submission through events-form block; chrono-box conditionally suppresses first schedule item when no conditions match.
nodes.details: The sessions-hub block now triggers auto-registration by delegating form submission to the events-form block rather than handling RSVP directly. This pattern centralizes form field validation and payload preparation in events-form. Additionally, chrono-box (timing-framework) implements conditional rendering: the first schedule item is skipped if no time-condition rules match, preventing empty or placeholder schedule displays. Both patterns live in event-libs/v1/blocks/ and should be followed when extending RSVP or schedule rendering flows.

nodes.summary: EMC's per-option RSVP UI state model does not map cleanly to the event API's flat rsvpFormFields structure
nodes.details: The Event Management Console maintains granular per-option UI state for RSVP fields, while the underlying event API only exposes coarser visible/required flags on rsvpFormFields. This impedance mismatch requires a translation layer or dual-source loading strategy on the frontend. Future pods touching RSVP field configuration should budget time to handle this gap explicitly rather than assuming API parity.

nodes.summary: Consent suite visibility and country-region capture follow a locale-aware, metadata-driven pattern: force-consent-collection metadata controls suite visibility; country picker data-country-code maps to payload.countryRegion; consent index URL uses locale-prefixed fallback pattern matching promotional-content.
nodes.details: In events-form.js, the consent suite (country picker + terms) is conditionally rendered based on user type (guest) OR force-consent-collection metadata being true. Country pre-selection logic runs whenever the suite is present. The consent query index JSON is fetched via getConsentQueryIndexUrl() using getLocale() + FALLBACK_LOCALES pattern (same as promotional-content), not a static URL. On form submit, the selected country option's data-country-code attribute is extracted and sent as payload.countryRegion in the baseAttendee object; BASE_ATTENDEE_DATA_FILTER already whitelists this field. This establishes the contract: force-consent-collection is a boolean metadata flag that overrides guest-only consent visibility, and country selection always populates countryRegion when the suite is shown.

nodes.summary: Event form boolean toggles (showSponsors) default to true on creation and use ?? true fallback on load to handle omitted API fields.
nodes.details: When restoring or initializing event form state, boolean visibility toggles like showSponsors must default to true in EventFormContext and use nullish coalescing (?? true) in eventFormMappers.ts during load to gracefully handle API responses that omit the field. The payload serialization via buildEventPayload and EVENT_DATA_FILTER already includes the field when set; the mapper ensures the UI layer has a consistent default. This pattern applies to other optional boolean fields controlling detail-page visibility.

nodes.summary: Sponsors (Partners) are a separate entity tied to series; sponsorType field differentiates T1/T2 events from T3 events, which must use 'Partner' as the sponsorType value.
nodes.details: Sponsors are managed as a first-class resource with dedicated CRUD routes (src/routes/sponsors/*) and can be associated with events via sponsorType. The sponsorsMgr.js manager handles sponsor lifecycle. When linking a sponsor to an event, the sponsorType field acts as a version discriminator: T1 and T2 events use legacy sponsorType values, while T3 events must explicitly use sponsorType='Partner'. This separation enables sponsor hub pages (series-level sponsor galleries) independent of individual event associations. See src/routes/events/sponsors/* for event-sponsor linking and src/managers/sponsorsMgr.js for the data model.

nodes.summary: Event Form uses 4-step wizard structure where Step 1 groups 5 logical components (format, tags, info, dates, venue) rather than separating into individual steps; this matches v1 reference and improves UX.
nodes.details: The EventForm wizard in EMC follows a deliberate 4-step structure (not 8) where Step 1 contains EventFormatComponent, Tags, Event Info, Date/Time, and Venue components as logical sub-sections. This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: Do not omit detailPagePath from event PUT payloads; instead, use dataFilters to toggle submittable: true when title changes, coordinating with backend OpenAPI spec updates.
nodes.details: When updating an event via ESL PUT, detailPagePath was previously omitted because the backend marked it read-only. However, title changes require a new detailPagePath (new DA page). The fix: in useEventFormSave.ts, call dataFilters to set detailPagePath.submittable = true before the PUT, and detect title changes to trigger the DA page path dialog. This requires coordinated backend changes to the OpenAPI spec to allow the field in PUT requests. The anti-pattern is assuming a read-only field can never be submitted; instead, use conditional submittability flags in dataFilters based on business logic (e.g., title mutation).

nodes.summary: MPS integration manager handles marketing consent transmission and service-token generation with deferred routing integration pending guest-checkout flow.
nodes.details: The `mpsMgr.js` module in events-service-platform encapsulates two responsibilities: (1) sending marketing communication permissions to MPS, distinguishing implicit vs. explicit consent flows, and (2) generating and caching service tokens for the ESP client ID `acom_event_service`. The manager is implemented but not yet wired into `src/routes/attendees/create.js` because it depends on a pending guest-checkout flow. The current contract expects request bodies to include `consentId` and `contactMethod` (comma-separated channel list for explicit consent); these field names are subject to change pending stakeholder review (cc @cod87753). Future integrators should treat this as a blocking dependency on guest-checkout completion before routing attendee-create requests through mpsMgr.

nodes.summary: Country field defaulting follows a strict priority order: consentStringId > IMS profile countryCode > cookie > navigator.language (only when locale has region).

Use the synchronous findOptionByCountryCode helper to locate matching options. This prevents leaving the field empty and ensures attendee consent data is never lost during form personalization.

nodes.summary: Speaker photo hydration requires explicit imagesMgr.list() join; photos are stored as separate DynamoDB records (sk: imagekind#speaker-photo) and must be fetched and attached to speaker objects.

nodes.summary: requiresSxswTicket is stored on attendee records but intentionally does not sync to Splash; form availability is gated at console level, not API level.

It is accepted and stored as-is on attendee records via POST events/{eventId}/attendees and POST attendees endpoints, and returned in GET responses. Critically, this field is NOT included in Splash custom field mappings — it remains local to the events platform. Field visibility/requirement is controlled by Event Marketers at the console level (not API-enforced), meaning the API accepts the field regardless of event cloud-type. This establishes the boundary: events-service-platform owns storage and retrieval; console owns form presentation logic; Splash integration is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.summary: Event Title and EN Title fields have a 150-character max length constraint; this is a UI-enforced limit that likely mirrors a backend validation rule.
nodes.details: The EventInfoComponent.tsx form enforces a 150-character maximum on both the localized Event Title field and the English title for page URL field. This constraint should be treated as a durable API contract—any backend validation (in events-service-platform or events-service-layer) likely enforces the same 150-char boundary. When building PUT/POST payloads for event creation/update, truncate or validate titles to ≤150 chars before submission to avoid silent failures or backend rejection.

nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: Manager classes in events-service-platform automatically persist request body fields via spread operator; schema changes alone are sufficient for new optional fields without code changes.

This pattern applies to sponsor creation, updates, and retrieval. When adding optional fields to event entities, verify the manager uses spread semantics before adding schema-only changes.

nodes.summary: Session form dirty-state tracking and unsaved-changes dialog: parent components receive `sessionHasOpenForm` prop to gate navigation; SessionForm detects dirty state and triggers callbacks; FormWizard integrates confirmation dialog before allowing navigation away.
nodes.details: The session management enhancement establishes a pattern for handling unsaved changes across the EventForm hierarchy. SessionManagementComponent tracks form state via `sessionHasOpenForm` prop and notifies parents of changes. SessionForm is responsible for detecting dirty state (form modifications) and invoking callbacks to signal this state upward. FormWizard consumes this signal and blocks navigation by rendering a confirmation dialog before allowing users to leave the form. This pattern ensures data loss prevention across nested form components without losing the ability to navigate intentionally. Apply this pattern to other multi-step forms in EMC that risk data loss on navigation.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.

The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: Scope configs unify RSVP forms, locales, and custom attributes under a single typed config system with scope-inherited hierarchy (org → team) and full-replace merge semantics.

This pattern groups related fields (e.g., all basic event metadata in Step 1) while keeping the overall flow concise. Step 2 handles Speakers/Hosts, Step 3 handles images, Step 4 handles RSVP/status. When implementing new event forms or extending this wizard, maintain this grouping: do not split Step 1 into separate steps unless UX research shows users abandon multi-step forms at >6 steps. The FormWizard shared component manages progress tracking and navigation across all steps.

nodes.summary: Do not use Kinesis payload as source of truth for event metadata; always rehydrate from DynamoDB on every stream record, even for localization-only updates.
nodes.details: EMC emits two Kinesis records per event save (one for event, one for localization), but only the first carries full metadata (e.g., cloud-type). In EventDataStreamProcessor.js processRecord(), the prior logic conditionally rehydrated from DynamoDB only when liveUpdate=true, causing localization records to forward partial payloads downstream. This broke `.page` preview RSVP forms when the second (partial) write overwrote the first (complete) write. Fix: always rebuild newData.itemData from liveData (DynamoDB), falling back to Kinesis payload only for localizations and localizationOverrides fields. This ensures both eventData and localization Kinesis records produce fully hydrated payloads to Hoolihan/AIO DA.

nodes.summary: Scope configs support optional admin-set `label` field; UI falls back to `humanReadableType(type)` when label is absent, with raw type shown as muted secondary text.
nodes.details: The `label` field is optional in `Config` and `ConfigCreateBody` OpenAPI schemas. Frontend renders `label ?? humanReadableType(type)` in the configs table (label in bold, type as muted secondary). The `humanReadableType()` helper converts camelCase type names to title case (e.g., `rsvp` → RSVP, `customAttributes` → Custom Attributes). Label is added to `SYSTEM_KEYS` to prevent KeyValueEditor from surfacing it as a raw field. Both Create and Edit modals include a Label TextField; Create omits it from payload if blank. Custom attribute items also support a label field between Name and Type rows in CustomAttributesEditor.

nodes.summary: PhoneNumber and AttendeeTextField validation rules were relaxed to accept legacy user-typed formats in the database; request and response validation kept symmetric pending future RSVP form redesign and data normalization.
nodes.details: In openapi.json, PhoneNumber pattern changed from `^\+?[0-9]+$` to `^\+?[0-9 ().-]+$` (maxLength 20→30) to accept spaces, parens, and dashes; AttendeeTextField maxLength raised from 100 to 200 across 10 fields (companyName, organizationName, dietaryRestrictions, invitedBy, etc.). This was a production blocker: 13% of ~1,650 attendee records violated the stricter MWPW-188918 rules, causing GET /v1/events/{eventId}/attendees to fail express-openapi-validator with HTTP 418. Request and response validation were kept symmetric intentionally—future phone canonicalization or RSVP form validation tightening can re-constrain the spec independently. Data normalization (216 malformed phones) is out of scope and tracked separately.

nodes.summary: Parallel API queries for attendee status types are merged into a single result set; new status types require only type union updates and StatusBadge entries, not table/filter/export logic changes.
nodes.details: In EMC's Registrations page, attendee statuses (registered, waitlisted, declined) are fetched via parallel `?type=X` queries in `getAllEventAttendees()` (web-src/src/services/api.ts) and merged into a single `AttendeeStats` result. The `RegistrationStatus` type union (web-src/src/types/attendee.ts) controls which statuses exist. Adding a new status requires: (1) extending the `RegistrationStatus` union, (2) adding a `StatusBadge` variant entry (web-src/src/components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx), and (3) updating `AttendeeStats` interface. Table rendering, filtering, and CSV export are data-driven and automatically support new statuses without code changes.

nodes.summary: Dev token system is gated by both URL query parameter (?devtokenmode=true) and host allowlist (localhost or approved dev instances); without the parameter, the UI button is hidden and stored tokens are not used for API calls.
nodes.details: The dev token feature in EMC requires two conditions to be active: (1) the URL must include ?devtokenmode=true and (2) the host must be localhost or an approved dev instance (e.g., 14257-emc-dev.adobeio-static.net). When both conditions are met, the Dev Token button appears in the top-right UI and API calls use the stored token via tokenStorage.getValidToken(). When running in Adobe Experience Cloud Shell, the real IMS token is automatically used instead and the dev token button never appears. API calls should use constructRequestHeaders(token) and safeFetch() helpers to inject the token into request headers.

nodes.summary: RSVP field option panels render inline within the field card with conditional icon toggle; drag interactions collapse all open panels to enforce mutual exclusivity.
nodes.details: In RegistrationFieldsComponent.tsx, option panels for RSVP fields (select, multi-select) now render as children inside the field card border rather than as sibling elements below. The expand/collapse trigger is a ListBulleted icon in a 5th grid column (only rendered for fields with selectable options via rsvpFieldDefinitions.ts). The icon highlights in selection-ring color when open. Starting a field drag operation collapses all open option panels—this is a deliberate UX constraint to prevent simultaneous drag and panel interactions. Option rows no longer have individual borders; drag-over ring feedback is retained. Fields without options have no list icon and no extra column gap.

nodes.summary: Do not assume rsvpData arrival timing relative to async attendee personalization; subscribe before async work and re-check after await to avoid race conditions in RSVP state transitions.
nodes.details: In event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js, rsvpData subscriptions must be established before initiating async personalization flows (e.g., attendee profile fetches). After awaiting async work, re-check the RSVP status to ensure registered/waitlisted state is captured even if the status update arrived during the async operation. This pattern prevents users from landing on incorrect form states when RSVP confirmations race with personalization. The profile.js preload fallback writes should also be hardened to ensure consistent state. See test/unit/blocks/events-form/events-form.test.js and test/unit/scripts/profile.test.js for regression test patterns.

nodes.summary: POI (point of interest) must not be auto-hydrated into event objects for SharePoint push; responsibility lies with event marketers and FE validation.
nodes.details: PR #633 attempted to add POI to hydrated event objects in ServiceProcessor.js (aws/templates/lambda/events-kinesis-processor/src/ServiceProcessor.js) for SharePoint sync. This was reverted because: (1) event marketers are responsible for consciously excluding POI from form field selections during event creation, and (2) the EMC console FE (owned by Qiyun) provides safeguarding at RSVP field selection, where POI option visibility is already controlled. Do not auto-inject POI into the event hydration pipeline; enforce the contract that POI inclusion is an explicit, user-driven choice at form design time.

nodes.details: Implemented by fe-agent-registration: The RSVP form schema has a base layer (field types, ordering, validation rules) and per-locale overlays that override only label and placeholder strings. The FormRenderer selects the overlay matching the user's locale, falling back to the base layer. This keeps form structure consistent across locales while allowing full translation of user-facing text.

Direct API calls (e.g., from third-party integrations or curl) bypassed validation entirely. One test submission had an email field with 'not-an-email'. nodes.summary: EMC frontend organizes event form as 13 modular components under EventForm/ directory, each owning a logical section (venue, speakers, agenda, etc.), composed by EventForm.tsx wizard container.
nodes.details: The EventForm/ directory contains 13 specialized components (EventFormatComponent, EventInfoComponent, VenueComponent, SpeakersComponent, SponsorsComponent, AgendaComponent, EventImagesComponent, ProfilesComponent, RegistrationConfigComponent, RegistrationFieldsComponent, PageMetadataComponent, plus index.ts barrel export) that are composed into a multi-step wizard by the parent EventForm.tsx container. Each component owns a logical domain (e.g., VenueComponent handles Google Places integration, SpeakersComponent manages speaker CRUD, RegistrationFieldsComponent configures RSVP form fields). This modular decomposition enables independent testing, reuse, and maintenance of form sections. The barrel export (index.ts) centralizes imports for the parent wizard.

nodes.summary: Event creation-to-publish time is the key organizer productivity metric — target under 15 minutes
nodes.details: Analysis by pm-lead: Tracking data from the existing EMC shows average event creation-to-publish time of 35 minutes. Most time is spent on session scheduling and RSVP form configuration. Reducing this to 15 minutes requires: (1) cloning from templates, (2) default configs at org level, (3) bulk session creation. These insights should inform the Sessions and Configs pods.

nodes.summary: Scope configs unify RSVP forms, locales, and custom attributes under a single typed config system with scope-inherited hierarchy (org → team) and full-replace merge semantics.
nodes.details: All configuration for the events console — RSVP form fields, locale definitions, and custom attribute definitions — is managed through a single `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs` API with `type` field (e.g., 'rsvp', 'locales', 'custom-attributes'). Configs inherit down the scope hierarchy with full-replace merge per type. Frontend reads merged configs via `GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs` or `GET /v1/series/{seriesId}/configs` with optional `?type=` filter. Custom attributes are a config type, not a separate entity. Admin management uses POST/PUT/DELETE on `/v1/scopes/{scopeId}/configs/{configId}` and requires `config:read`, `config:write`, or `config:delete` permissions.

nodes.summary: RSVP and custom attribute option values use { value, label } pairs: value is the locale-independent DB key, label is the localizable display text.
nodes.details: RSVP form field options and custom attribute values now follow a two-part structure: `value` (immutable, locale-independent identifier used for DB storage and API contracts) and `label` (localizable, user-facing display text). RsvpLocalizationsEditor matches translated options by value key rather than positional index, ensuring localization stability across option reordering. FieldOptionsEditor and CustomAttributesEditor both support bulk edit and semicolon-paste workflows. This pattern applies across console/src/components/configs/ (ScopeConfigsView.jsx, FieldOptionsEditor, RsvpLocalizationsEditor, CustomAttributesEditor) and test fixtures (addRsvpConfig.js, addCustomAttributesConfig.js).

nodes.summary: Scope configs (rsvp, locales, customAttributes) are the authoritative source for event metadata; publishing profiles are deprecated but retained for backward compatibility during migration.
nodes.details: Events created under Creative Events (25f26faa-f8e2-4e99-b341-81a3995ef9af) and Enterprise Events (d758a3bc-ff31-4bfe-a2f5-343f074aec6c) scopes must define four config types: rsvp (pool of form fields), locales (localeNames, localeUrlCodes), and customAttributes (with primaryProductName and promotionalItems attributes). The Kinesis processor (events-kinesis-processor/ServiceProcessor.applyRelatedData) must call GET /v1/events/{eventId}/configs to hydrate event.locales, event.customAttributesConfig, and event.rsvpConfig at stream-processing time; event DDB records store only user selections (rsvpFormFields, customAttributes[] with valueId), not full definitions. Publishing profiles remain in the payload for backward compat but are no longer the source of truth. hoolihan-webhooks must read primary product from event.customAttributes[] where attribute='primaryProductName', promotional items from customAttributes[] where attribute='promotionalItems', RSVP pool from event.rsvpConfig.rsvpFormFields[], and locales from event.locales.localeNames/localeUrlCodes.

nodes.summary: RSVP form field configuration requires option-level granularity (subset selection, ordering) that is non-trivial on the BE and easy to underestimate
nodes.details: The assumption that rsvpFormFields could be manipulated at the field level was insufficient — option-level control (enabling/disabling individual options, reordering them) required separate, unplanned BE work. Any pod touching RSVP or dynamic form-field configuration should scope BE option-level support as an explicit, separate work item.

nodes.summary: RSVP registration payloads must include `requiresSxswTicket` flag and implicit consent via `contactMethods` field; sanitize HTML in form text/textarea inputs and enforce RSVP limit column as maxlength constraint.
nodes.details: When submitting event-attendee payloads for RSVP, include `requiresSxswTicket` boolean when SXSW ticket filter applies (#140). Implicit consent for new registrations is recorded via the `contactMethods` field in the payload (MWPW-194036, #126). In events-form block (event-libs/v1/blocks/events-form/events-form.js), sanitize HTML in text and textarea inputs (#110) and honor the RSVP limit column value as the `maxlength` attribute constraint. These patterns ensure consistent registration data shape and prevent XSS while respecting capacity limits.

nodes.summary: Per-resource PUT payload sanitizers live in utils/dataFilters.ts and follow prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload naming
nodes.details: Convention adopted across the EMC frontend: every ESP PUT endpoint has a corresponding prepareEsp{Resource}PutPayload function in web-src/src/utils/dataFilters.ts that calls filterSeriesData (or the resource-specific equivalent) in 'update' mode. This centralizes read-only-field stripping and ensures unpublish, archive, and external-update flows all go through the same validation layer. Do not invent ad-hoc filtering at the call site.

nodes.summary: Sessions-hub auto-registration integrates RSVP form submission through events-form block; chrono-box conditionally suppresses first schedule item when no conditions match.
nodes.details: The sessions-hub block now triggers auto-registration by delegating form submission to the events-form block rather than handling RSVP directly. This pattern centralizes form field validation and payload preparation in events-form. Additionally, chrono-box (timing-framework) implements conditional rendering: the first schedule item is skipped if no time-condition rules match, preventing empty or placeholder schedule displays. Both patterns live in event-libs/v1/blocks/ and should be followed when extending RSVP or schedule rendering flows.

nodes.summary: EMC dark mode uses system prefers-color-scheme via usePreferredColorScheme hook, syncs React Spectrum 2 colorScheme prop, and defines semantic CSS tokens (--emc-field-*, --emc-event-form-shell-bg) that mirror compiled S2 Field colors (dark #111 fill, #444 border) under both @media and html[data-color-scheme] selectors for hydration safety.
nodes.details: The usePreferredColorScheme hook (web-src/src/hooks/usePreferredColorScheme.ts) subscribes to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and sets document.documentElement.dataset.colorScheme, which is passed to S2Provider colorScheme prop in App/AuthGate/RBACGate. index.css defines light :root defaults and dark @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) overrides for both legacy --spectrum-global-* and new semantic tokens (--emc-field-bg, --emc-field-border, --emc-field-focus-ring). Tokens are duplicated under html[data-color-scheme='dark'] selector to ensure first paint and post-effect hydration alignment. Custom controls (Quill RTE via .rte-field-shell, Google Places venue field via .emc-field-like) suppress UA outline and use :focus-visible for keyboard focus rings while relying on border changes for mouse focus, matching S2 behavior. designSystem.ts SURFACES enum (shell/card/format-dialog) centralizes surface-level background tokens.

nodes.summary: IMS user context must be threaded as a prop through component tree (App → UserPanel, SideBar); UserPanel displays profile data with graceful fallback when IMS profile unavailable.
nodes.details: The UserPanel component receives an `ims` prop containing `{ profile?: IMSProfile, org?: string, token?: string }` where IMSProfile has `userId`, `name`, `email`. Components extract user context via optional chaining (e.g., `ims.profile?.name || 'Guest'`). When `ims.profile` is absent, UserPanel renders 'Not Connected' state. This pattern establishes the contract for how IMS data flows through the EMC frontend: App.tsx passes `ims` to both UserPanel and SideBar, and any component needing user context receives the same IMS object structure. Token is never rendered; user ID is truncated in UI for privacy.

nodes.summary: All DELETE endpoints return 204 No Content; all database managers export singleton instances; event images are a first-class resource with full CRUD routes.
nodes.details: DELETE operations across all routes (eventSeries/delete.js, events/delete.js, events/attendees/delete.js, events/speakers/delete.js, events/images/delete.js) now return HTTP 204 No Content instead of 200 with an empty array. All manager classes in src/managers/ (attendeesMgr.js, eventsMgr.js, seriesMgr.js, speakersMgr.js, venuesMgr.js) export a singleton instance rather than the class itself, requiring route handlers to call methods on the exported instance. Event images are now a managed resource with dedicated CRUD routes (src/routes/events/images/) backed by database implementation in eventsMgr.js.

recentUpdates.summary: Three config types at scope level: RSVP form fields, Locales, Custom Attributes
recentUpdates.details: Decision: the config service manages three config types, all scoped to org or team level. (1) RSVP form fields: defines which fields appear on registration forms, with localization overlays for label/placeholder per locale. (2) Locales: list of supported locales for the scope with URL codes. (3) Custom Attributes: single-select, multi-select, or text input fields with ordered value lists. Each config type is independently versioned and cached.

recentUpdates.summary: ConfigService singleton with 5-minute cache TTL, 2 retries, and request deduplication
recentUpdates.details: ConfigService is a singleton (one instance per server process). Caches resolved configs for 5 minutes. On cache miss, retries up to 2 times with 500ms backoff. Request deduplication: if multiple callers request the same config simultaneously, only one API call is made and the result is shared. Cache key: scope_type:scope_id:config_type.

recentUpdates.summary: Config CRUD endpoints complete with full-replace inheritance — child scope completely replaces parent
recentUpdates.details: Implemented GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /configs/:scopeType/:scopeId/:configType. Inheritance: when resolving a config, the service checks team-level first; if not found, falls back to org-level. This is full-replace — a team config completely replaces the org config, no field-level merging. Permissions: config:read for GET, config:write for POST/PUT, config:delete for DELETE. All endpoints integrated with ConfigService cache.

recentUpdates.summary: PM requests deep-merge inheritance: team configs should only specify overrides, not duplicate all org fields
recentUpdates.details: Feedback from event organizer interviews: teams want to add 2-3 custom RSVP fields without re-specifying all 15 base fields from the org config. With full-replace, every team must copy the full org config and append their additions. When the org updates a base field (e.g., changes 'Company' label to 'Organization'), teams don't see the change unless they manually update their copy. Deep-merge would solve this.

recentUpdates.summary: RSVP config editor with localization overlay UI
recentUpdates.details: Built the RSVP config editor. Users can add/remove/reorder form fields. Each field has a base label/placeholder and locale-specific overrides displayed in a tabbed overlay panel. Locale tabs are driven by the Locales config for the current scope. Custom Attributes editor shows single-select, multi-select, and text input types with drag-to-reorder value lists.

recentUpdates.summary: Blocked on inheritance model decision — cannot proceed with config resolution refactor until C-301 is resolved
recentUpdates.details: If deep-merge wins, the ConfigService resolution logic needs a complete rewrite: (1) fetch both org and team configs, (2) deep-merge with team taking precedence, (3) handle ordered list merging for custom attribute values (append? replace? interleave?), (4) update cache invalidation to bust both scope levels when either changes. Estimated 2-3 days of work. Cannot start until the decision is made.

recentUpdates.summary: ConfigService cache: 5-minute TTL is sufficient for config read patterns
recentUpdates.details: Analyzed config read patterns from the existing EMC deployment. Configs are read ~500 times per minute across all scopes. Config writes happen ~3 times per day per scope. The 5-minute TTL means a worst-case 5-minute delay for config changes to propagate, which is acceptable given the write frequency. Real-time invalidation would require an event bus (SNS/SQS or WebSocket) which adds operational complexity.

recentUpdates.summary: Request: config writes should immediately reflect in the editing user's UI
recentUpdates.details: When an admin saves RSVP config changes, the preview panel should show the updated config immediately — not after up to 5 minutes. Proposal: the POST/PUT response should return the saved config, and the frontend should update its local cache/state from the response. This doesn't require server-side cache invalidation — just a write-through pattern on the client.
